+---
+title: How to Find CubeSandbox Component Logs (cubecli logs and the Guest Kernel Log)
+author: ls-ggg
+date: 2026-07-15
+tags:
+  - logging
+  - cubelet
+  - cubeshim
+  - operations
+lang: en-US
+---
+
+# How to Find CubeSandbox Component Logs (cubecli logs and the Guest Kernel Log)
+
+## Symptom
+
+CubeSandbox is made up of several components (CubeAPI, CubeMaster, Cubelet, CubeShim, the Hypervisor/VMM, network-agent, cube-proxy). When troubleshooting, it's often unclear which log file a given error actually lands in, where the guest kernel boot log can be found, and how to raise Cubelet's log verbosity — its default log level (`warn`) doesn't print enough detail to reproduce most issues.
+
+This article lists the **exact paths** for every component's logs in a one-click (systemd-managed) deployment, explains how to use `cubecli logs` to read sandbox/template logs, shows where the guest kernel boot log lives, and covers how to turn on Cubelet debug logging.
+
+## Environment
+
+- Cube Sandbox version: v0.4.0 or newer (one-click deployment, systemd-managed)
+- Deployment mode: all-in-one or multi-node cluster, applies to both
+- Host OS / kernel: any Linux host running Cubelet
+- Related components: CubeAPI, CubeMaster, Cubelet, CubeShim, Hypervisor (VMM), network-agent, cube-proxy
+
+## Root Cause
+
+CubeSandbox logs fall into three categories, each with a different source and a different way to read it:
+
+1. **Business/behavioral logs**: requests, scheduling, audit, VMM creation, etc. Each component writes these directly to files under `/data/log/<Module>/`. They **never** show up in `journalctl`.
+2. **Startup-time logs**: the stdout/stderr produced while a process is being brought up by systemd (or exiting on failure). These can only be viewed with `journalctl -u <unit>`.
+3. **Sandbox/template container logs**: the stdout/stderr of the sandbox's init process (container PID 1), written by CubeShim into Cubelet's private mount namespace. These require `cubecli logs` to read; template build logs, by contrast, land on the host filesystem and need no namespace entry.
+
+The guest kernel's boot log is, at its core, just another form of "container init process output": CubeShim forwards everything the guest kernel prints over its `console=hvc0` console — including the `Linux version ...` boot banner — into the very same `cube-shim-req.log`. So **the guest kernel log is already inside the CubeShim log**; no extra tooling is needed.
+
+Cubelet defaults to a fairly quiet `warn` log level, so normal operation won't print detailed debug information. There are two ways to raise it to `debug`: edit the hot-reloaded dynamic config file, or flip it temporarily via a built-in HTTP endpoint (no restart required).
+
+## Solution
+
+### 1. Component log cheat sheet
+
+| Component | Log type | Path | How to view |
+|---|---|---|---|
+| CubeAPI | Business request log (daily rotation) | `/data/log/CubeAPI/cube-api-YYYY-MM-DD.log` | `tail -F` |
+| CubeMaster | Business request log | `/data/log/CubeMaster/cubemaster-req.log` | `tail -F` |
+| CubeMaster | Startup-time log | `/data/log/CubeMaster/cubemaster.log` | `tail -F` |
+| Cubelet | Business request log | `/data/log/Cubelet/Cubelet-req.log` | `tail -F` |
+| Cubelet | Stats/metrics log | `/data/log/Cubelet/Cubelet-stat.log` | `tail -F` |
+| Cubelet | Startup-time log | — | `journalctl -u cube-sandbox-cubelet.service` |
+| CubeShim | Business request log (includes guest kernel output) | `/data/log/CubeShim/cube-shim-req.log` | `tail -F` |
+| CubeShim | Stats log | `/data/log/CubeShim/cube-shim-stat.log` | `tail -F` |
+| Hypervisor (VMM) | VMM creation log | `/data/log/CubeVmm/vmm.log` | `tail -F` |
+| network-agent | Business request log | `/data/log/network-agent/network-agent-req.log` | `tail -F` |
+| cube-proxy | Access/error/sidecar logs (inside container) | container-internal `/data/log/cube-proxy/{access,error,sidecar}.log` | `docker exec <container> tail ...` (see below) |
+| Sandbox container | init process stdout/stderr | `/data/cubelet/state/io.containerd.runtime.v2.task/default/<sandbox-id>/{stdout,stderr}` (inside Cubelet's mount namespace) | `cubecli logs <sandbox-id>` (see below) |
+| Template build | Build container stdout/stderr | `/data/log/template/<template-id>_0/{stdout,stderr}` (host filesystem) | `cubecli logs --tpl <template-id>` |
+
+::: tip Business logs are not in journalctl
+As also documented in `docs/guide/service-management.md`: all business/request logs above go **directly to files under `/data/log/<Module>/`**. `journalctl` only shows the small amount of stdout/stderr produced while the process is starting up or exiting.
+:::
+
+### 2. Reading sandbox / template logs with `cubecli logs`
+
+`cubecli` is built alongside Cubelet and installed automatically by the one-click installer. Sandbox log files live inside Cubelet's private mount namespace, so `cubecli logs` **must be run directly on the compute node** — it cannot be invoked remotely via any API.
+
+```bash
+# Sandbox stdout, last 100 lines (default)
+cubecli logs <sandbox-id>
+
+# Sandbox stderr, last 100 lines
+cubecli logs --stderr <sandbox-id>
+
+# Full sandbox log
+cubecli logs --all <sandbox-id>
+
+# Last N / first N lines
+cubecli logs --tail 50 <sandbox-id>
+cubecli logs --head 20 <sandbox-id>
+
+# Template build log: read straight from the host filesystem, skipping namespace entry
+cubecli logs --tpl <template-id>
+cubecli logs --tpl --all --stderr <template-id>
+```
+
+Flags:
+
+| Flag | Shorthand | Description |
+|---|---|---|
+| `--tpl` | — | Treat the id as a template ID, reading from `/data/log/template/<id>_0/` with no namespace entry |
+| `--stderr` | `-e` | Read stderr instead of stdout |
+| `--all` | `-a` | Print all lines; cannot be combined with `--tail`/`--head` |
+| `--tail N` | `-t N` | Print the last N lines (default 100) |
+| `--head N` | `-H N` | Print the first N lines |
+
+`cubecli logs` only covers the output of the **container init process (PID 1)**. Sub-tasks started inside a sandbox via the E2B `exec` interface produce their own stdout/stderr, which must be captured with the E2B SDK's `on_stdout`/`on_stderr` callbacks — that's out of scope here; see [Sandbox Logs](../sandbox-logs.md).
+
+Log files are removed together with the sandbox once it's deleted, and log forwarding requires CubeShim v0.4.0 or newer.
+
+### 3. Guest kernel log: right there in the CubeShim log
+
+When CubeShim boots a VM, it takes over the guest kernel's console output via the `console=hvc0` kernel parameter, and — just like the sandbox's init-process output — forwards it into the same CubeShim request log file:
+
+```bash
+sudo grep -a "<sandbox-id or InstanceId>" /data/log/CubeShim/cube-shim-req.log | grep -a "Linux version"
+```
+
+`cube-shim-req.log` is newline-delimited JSON; the actual log text lives in the `LogContent` field. A typical guest kernel boot record looks like:
+
+```json
+{"Module":"Shim","InstanceId":"<sandbox-id>","ContainerId":"<sandbox-id>","Timestamp":"...","LogContent":"[    0.000000] Linux version 6.12.33-cube.sandbox.pvm.guest-... #2 SMP PREEMPT_DYNAMIC ...","FunctionType":""}
+```
+
+Filtering by `InstanceId` (the sandbox ID) gets you the full kernel boot output for that sandbox — device probing, `EXT4-fs`, rootfs mount, and so on — with no extra tooling or namespace entry required.
+
+::: tip Why it's here and not somewhere else
+`console=hvc0` is the VM's serial console; every kernel `printk` goes through it. CubeShim forwards that console stream straight into its own log pipeline (sharing the same writer as its ordinary request logs), so reading the guest kernel log is just a `grep` on `cube-shim-req.log` — no extra mount or debug tool needed.
+:::
+
+### 4. cube-proxy's in-container logs
+
+`cube-proxy` is an OpenResty-based nginx container. Its logs live inside the container at `/data/log/cube-proxy/`, **not on the host filesystem**, so you need `docker exec` to read them:
+
+```bash
+docker exec -it cube-proxy tail /data/log/cube-proxy/error.log
+docker exec -it cube-proxy tail /data/log/cube-proxy/sidecar.log
+docker exec -it cube-proxy tail /data/log/cube-proxy/access.log
+```
+
+The container name is fixed at `cube-proxy` (created by systemd via `docker create`); you can confirm the actual container name/ID with `docker ps` first if needed.
+
+| File | Content |
+|---|---|
+| `access.log` | nginx access log |
+| `error.log` | nginx error log |
+| `sidecar.log` | cube-proxy sidecar logic (auth/routing, etc.) |
+
+### 5. Enabling Cubelet debug-level logging
+
+Cubelet's default log level is `warn`, which usually isn't verbose enough for troubleshooting. There are two ways to raise it to `debug`, neither of which requires **restarting the Cubelet process**:
+
+#### Option 1: Edit the dynamic config file (persistent, hot-reloaded)
+
+Cubelet polls its dynamic config file `dynamicconf/conf.yaml` every 10 seconds and hot-reloads it (including re-applying the log level) whenever it changes. Add a `log_level` line under the `common:` section:
+
+```yaml
+common:
+  enable_pf_mode: false
+  log_level: debug   # add this line
+  sandbox_exec_cmd_time_out: 5s
+  ...
+```
+
+In a one-click deployment, the default path for this file is:
+
+```
+/usr/local/services/cubetoolbox/Cubelet/dynamicconf/conf.yaml
+```
+
+After saving, wait roughly 10 seconds (the config poll interval) for Cubelet to pick up `debug` level; `/data/log/Cubelet/Cubelet-req.log` will then start emitting much finer-grained records. Remember to remove the line or reset it back to `info`/`warn` once you're done, so you don't accumulate excessive log volume long-term.
+
+#### Option 2: Flip it temporarily via the debug port (no file change, resets on restart)
+
+Cubelet exposes a built-in debug HTTP port (listening on `:9966` by default, matching `[debug] address` in `config.toml`) with a `/debug/loglevel` endpoint you can call directly to switch levels on the fly:
+
+```bash
+# Switch to debug
+curl -X POST 'http://127.0.0.1:9966/debug/loglevel?level=debug'
+
+# Switch back to info once done
+curl -X POST 'http://127.0.0.1:9966/debug/loglevel?level=info'
+```
+
+This takes effect immediately, with no polling delay — but it's **only valid for the lifetime of the current process**. Once Cubelet restarts, the level reverts to whatever the config file specifies (`warn` by default). This is the right choice when you want to capture a short window of detailed logs without touching the config file.
+
+The same debug port also hosts `pprof` profiling endpoints (`/debug/pprof/*`), which are useful when investigating performance issues.

## PR #963 — SDK Volume API Documentation (review)

### Overview
Good quality PR. The Volume API implementation (`_volume.py`) is cleanly factored, tests are thorough, and documentation is well-aligned. The notes below are the issues I consider worth acting on before merging.

---

### 1. `AuthenticationError` not publicly exported (docs/code mismatch)
**`sdk/python/cubesandbox/__init__.py` — all lines**

`docs/volume.md` and `docs/volume.zh.md` document that HTTP 401/403 raises `AuthenticationError`, and `_volume.py` does raise it. But `__init__.py` does **not** import or re-export `AuthenticationError`. Users who read the error table and try `from cubesandbox import AuthenticationError` get an `ImportError`.

Either add it to `__init__.py` (preferred, since it's already used elsewhere in the SDK) or note in the docs that it must be imported from the private module.

---

### 2. `X-API-Key` header not sent on sandbox endpoints
**`sdk/python/cubesandbox/sandbox.py` — lines 250-252 and all other control-plane calls**

`_auth_headers()` (defined in `_volume.py`) adds `X-API-Key` to Volume API calls, but `sandbox.py` does not send it on `Sandbox.create`, `Sandbox.list`, `Sandbox.connect`, etc. If CubeAPI is deployed with auth enabled, sandbox endpoints will return 401/403 while volume endpoints work.

If this is intentional (sandbox auth is separate), a docstring note would help future readers. Otherwise `_auth_headers` should be consistently applied.

---

### 3. `Volume.list` will crash on empty 204 response
**`sdk/python/cubesandbox/_volume.py:237`**

```python
data = resp.json() or []
```

If the server returns `204 No Content` (no body), `resp.json()` raises `JSONDecodeError` — the `_check_response` call on line 236 already passed for 2xx. Although unusual for a list endpoint, this is a realistic edge case. Consider adding a `204` guard or try/except.

---

### 4. `Volume.list(config)` docs show wrong signature
**`sdk/python/README.md:341`**, **`sdk/python/README.zh.md:338`**

Both README files show `Volume.list(config)`, but the actual signature is `def list(cls, *, config=None)` — `config` is keyword-only. The other Volume entries (`create`, `get`, `delete`) correctly use `*,` in the docs. Fix for consistency.

---

### 5. Chinese volume docs have a return-value detail table absent from English
**`sdk/python/docs/volume.zh.md` (new section) vs `sdk/python/docs/volume.md`**

The Chinese version includes a "返回值详解" table mapping each method's per-field availability. This is a genuine improvement over the English version, where the information is scattered. Consider adding the equivalent table to the English doc, positioned after the `Volume.create` parameter table.

---

### 6. `_check_response` double-parses `resp.json()`
**`sdk/python/cubesandbox/_volume.py:26`**

```python
msg = resp.json().get("message") or resp.json().get("detail") or resp.text
```

`resp.json()` is called twice on every error path — it's not cached. Consolidate to a single call: `body = resp.json(); msg = body.get("message") or body.get("detail") or resp.text`.

---

### 7. Missing test coverage for auth header & AuthenticationError path
**`sdk/python/tests/test_volume.py`**

- No unit test verifies `X-API-Key` header is sent/received when `api_key` is configured in the config.
- No test verifies HTTP 401/403 raises `AuthenticationError` (only 400/404/500 are tested).
- These are security-significant code paths that deserve coverage.

---

### 8. `VolumeInfo.from_dict` silently accepts empty/missing `volumeID`
**`sdk/python/cubesandbox/_volume.py:92-95`**

```python
volume_id=data.get("volumeID") or data.get("volume_id", ""),
```

If the server returns `"volumeID": ""` or omits the key, the result is `volume_id=""`. This could cascade into `Volume.get("")` hitting a malformed URL. Consider enforcing a non-empty `volume_id` at construction time.

### Minor notes (no action required):
- `requests.Session()` is created per-call (not reused) across the entire SDK — pre-existing pattern, not introduced here.
- Integration scenarios never exercise dict-style mounts — unit tests cover this, so low risk.

---

## Review: PR #961 – fix(web): keep sandbox state counts across filters

**Files changed:** 1 · `web/src/pages/Sandboxes.tsx` (+16 / -8)

### Summary

The PR correctly fixes the reported bug (#960). By always fetching the full sandbox list and applying the state filter client-side, badge counts now accurately reflect the full dataset regardless of which tab is active. The implementation is clean and introduces no correctness issues or security concerns.

### Positive aspects

- The `useMemo` dependency array (`[data, q, stateFilter]`) is complete — no stale closures.
- The guard clause `if (next === stateFilter) return;` prevents no-op updates on tab switch.
- Empty-state handling (`filtered.length === 0 && !isLoading`) is correctly placed.
- The `void refetch()` idiom correctly suppresses floating-promise lint warnings.

### Issues found

#### 1. Redundant `refetch()` on tab switch (line 37)

Calling `void refetch()` inside `onStateFilterChange` is unnecessary. Since:
- The query key is now `['sandboxes']` (no state filter), and
- The data is already polled every 5 seconds via `refetchInterval: 5_000`,

every tab switch fires an extra HTTP request for data that is already present and at most 5 seconds stale in the cache. For users who toggle between Running and Paused tabs, this multiplies backend load for zero data benefit.

**Recommendation:** Remove the `void refetch();` call. The filter is entirely client-side now, so tab switching is purely a UI state change.

#### 2. Inline badge counts recompute redundant O(n) passes (line 140)

```tsx
{data.filter((sb) => (sb.state ?? 'running') === key).length}
```

This filter runs on every render — once for the Running badge and once for the Paused badge — producing two full passes over `data` on each render cycle. Meanwhile, the `filtered` useMemo (line 66) is already doing a similar operation. For deployments with many sandboxes or the 5-second polling interval, this adds unnecessary render-time CPU cost.

**Recommendation:** Derive badge counts inside the existing `useMemo` alongside `filtered` to reduce render-phase work from 3 passes to 1 pass.

#### 3. Duplicated `sb.state ?? 'running'` default

The state-defaulting expression `sb.state ?? 'running'` appears in three places (lines 70, 140, 198). If the default or valid states ever change, all three must be updated in lockstep.

**Recommendation:** Extract a small helper (e.g. `const sandboxState = (sb: RunningSandbox) => sb.state ?? 'running'`) to centralize the default.

### Test coverage

The web frontend has no test infrastructure — no test runner, no test files, no test script. This PR fixes a bug that would have been caught by a simple unit test on the filtering pipeline (`data → stateFilter → search query → filtered rows`). Adding test coverage for the filtering and badge count logic would prevent similar regressions. However, this is a project-level gap, not a concern specific to this PR.

### Security

No security issues were identified — all data flows through proper authentication headers, all user-visible content is React-escaped, and no new attack surface is created. Safe to merge from a security perspective.

### Verdict

The fix is correct and addresses the root cause. The two actionable suggestions are:
1. **Recommended before merge:** Remove the redundant `refetch()` on tab switch (line 37).
2. **Nice to have:** Memoize badge counts to avoid redundant O(n) passes (line 140).

Merging as-is would not introduce a regression.

## Background

On the WebUI sandbox page, selecting the `Running` tab could make the `Paused` badge count disappear even when paused sandboxes still existed.

The page requested a state-filtered sandbox list and then calculated all status badge counts from that already-filtered response. As a result, switching tabs could make the badge counts reflect only the current tab instead of the full sandbox list.

## What Changed

* Fetch the full sandbox list for the page.
* Derive the `Running` and `Paused` badge counts from the full list.
* Apply the selected state filter locally to the table rows.
* Apply text search after the selected state filter.
* Refetch the full list immediately when switching state tabs, preserving the existing tab-switch refresh behavior.

The state filter is now local because badge counts need the full list. The explicit tab-change refetch is intentional, it preserves the previous immediate-refresh behavior, while the five-second polling interval remains the background refresh mechanism.

## Validation

* `npm ci --no-audit --no-fund`
* `npm run build`

  * includes TypeScript checking and the Vite production build
* `git diff --check`
* Manual validation:

  * ran `npm run dev`
  * configured the `/cubeapi` Vite proxy to CubeAPI
  * verified that switching between `All`, `Running`, and `Paused` keeps the paused badge count visible when `Running` is selected
  * verified that displayed rows still follow the selected state filter

## Related

Fixes #960.

1. **Line 50 — `0o755` should be `0o700`**: The mount point on line 64 uses `0o700` (owner-only), but the artifact directory uses `0o755` (world-readable). The final ext4 image is a full container rootfs. On a shared host, other processes could read it. Use `0o700` for consistency.

2. **Line 88 — Missing `--` separator**: `mount` and `losetup --detach` use `"--"` for argument/option separation, but this `losetup --find --show` call doesn't. Defense-in-depth.

3. **Line 158 — Unnecessary fork/exec for already-aligned sizes**: When `alignedSize == fsSize`, `truncate -s <sameSize>` is still forked. Add `if alignedSize != fsSize { ... }` guard.

---

### Additional findings

4. **`getFileBlockSize` is now dead code** (in `util.go`). The only caller was the old step 7 logic. The new code correctly uses `os.Stat().Size()` instead. Remove the function to avoid confusion and maintenance debt.

5. **Silent `os.Stat` failure in alignment step** (line 155). If `os.Stat(ext4Path)` fails, `fsSize` silently falls back to `estimatedSizeBytes`, which could be much larger than the post-resize2fs file — defeating the space savings and wasting guest memory address space. Consider logging the stat error so over-provisioning is observable.

6. **Test coverage gap**: The entire `createExt4ImageStreaming` function body is patched out with `gomonkey` in the three existing `TestBuildExt4Streaming*` tests. None of the three fixed bugs have regression tests. Particularly valuable would be:
   - A direct test for `createExt4ImageStreaming` with mocked `runCommand`/`exec.CommandContext`/`os.Stat`, including the losetup stderr-separation scenario (Bug 2).
   - A table-driven test for the alignment math (Bug 3) — this is pure logic and doesn't need external commands.
   - Coverage of the `os.MkdirAll` error path (Bug 1).

7. **`resize2fs -M` comment (line 147)**: The comment says `resize2fs -M` "truncates the file to the exact filesystem length". In practice `resize2fs -M` shrinks the filesystem **metadata** but may not truncate the backing file itself — the actual truncation happens in step 7. This is a minor clarification that could prevent confusion for future readers wondering why `fi.Size()` doesn't shrink after step 6.

---

item.body:
## Summary

`createExt4ImageStreaming` — the Phase-2 loop-mount rootfs build path gated by
`CUBEMASTER_LOOP_MOUNT_EXT4_ENABLED` — has three bugs. The first two make the
loop-mount path fail and silently fall back to the slow Phase-1
`mkfs.ext4 -d` build; the third builds fast but yields an artifact the compute
node refuses to boot.

## Bugs & fixes (all in `createExt4ImageStreaming`)

1. **Truncate before the store sub-dir exists → ENOENT.**
   The image is `truncate`d at `<store>/<artifact>/<artifact>.ext4` before that
   per-artifact directory exists (`ResolveArtifactStoreDir` only creates the
   `storage/` root; Phase-1 creates the sub-dir lazily during its `cp -a`
   relocate). The streaming path never relocates, so the truncate fails and the
   whole build falls back to Phase-1.
   **Fix:** `os.MkdirAll(filepath.Dir(ext4Path), 0o755)` before truncate.

2. **`losetup` stderr folded into the device path.**
   `losetup --find --show` is run with `CombinedOutput()`. losetup prints
   warnings to stderr (e.g. `Warning: file does not fit into a 512-byte sector;
   the end of the file will be ignored.`), which `CombinedOutput` merges into the
   returned string. The parsed `loopDevice` becomes a multiline value, so `mount`
   fails with exit 32 ("bad option"), and the same corrupt string breaks the
   deferred `losetup --detach`, leaking the loop device.
   **Fix:** capture stdout only via `cmd.Output()`, route stderr to a separate
   buffer used only for the error message.

3. **Final image not 2 MiB-aligned → boot rejected.**
   After `resize2fs -M`, the image is truncated to the filesystem length, which
   is only 512-byte aligned. The rootfs is later attached as a **virtio-pmem**
   device whose backing-file size must be a multiple of 2 MiB, otherwise the host
   device manager rejects it (`PmemSizeNotAligned`). Phase-1 avoids this for free
   because it sizes up to a 256 MiB boundary.
   **Fix:** round the apparent filesystem size **up** to 2 MiB before the final
   truncate. Rounding up never cuts into live filesystem blocks; the small tail
   is unused device space. Uses the apparent size (`os.Stat().Size()`), not
   `getFileBlockSize` (physically-allocated blocks), which can be smaller than
   the filesystem length for a minimized image and would truncate below it.

## Testing

Verified on a FUSE-mounted network filesystem artifact store, `from-image` build of a
`python:3.11-slim`-based template distributed to a bare-metal compute node:

- Phase-2 loop-mount path runs **end-to-end with no fallback** (0 "falling back
  to phase-1" warnings; `losetup`/`mount` show the loop device mounted at the
  streaming mount point).
- Build time **POST→READY ≈ 14 s** vs **~12 min** on Phase-1 for the same image
  on the same store (~50x; Phase-1 is dominated by per-small-file FUSE metadata
  round-trips during the `cp -a` relocate + `mkfs.ext4 -d` readback).
- Resulting artifact is **2 MiB-aligned** (e.g. 438304768 B = 418 MiB exactly)
  and the from-image job reaches **READY** — the compute node accepts the pmem
  device with **0** `PmemSizeNotAligned` errors.

<!-- cubesandbox-auto-review:start -->
## PR #956 Review: lifecycle: Sync pause/resume state from CubeMaster to CLM

Well-structured PR that addresses a real desynchronization problem. The hook pattern cleanly mirrors existing create/destroy hooks, tests are thorough, and most edge cases are considered. Below are the findings I consider worth addressing.

---

### Critical: TOCTOU race in `statesync.Handle` – non-atomic read-check-write (statesync/handler.go:102-127)

`GetState` reads the current state, the transition-marker check at line 114-120 evaluates it, and `SetState` at line 127 unconditionally overwrites — all without atomicity. The CLM's sweeper or resumer can SETNX a transition lock between the read and write, and `SetState` destroys it. A Lua script that atomically GET-and-SET only when the current value is a terminal state would fix this.

---

### High: Retry of proxy push is permanently blocked by idempotence check (statesync/handler.go:122-125)

If `SetState` succeeds but `ProxyPush.SetState` fails, a subsequent event redelivery hits `cur == newState` on line 123 and returns early — never retrying the proxy push. The CubeProxy per-worker state dict is then permanently desynchronized for that sandbox until an out-of-band mechanism (sweeper, polling) converges it. Proxy push should not be gated behind `cur == newState`.

---

### High: Head-of-line blocking in the stream consumer loop (main.go:302-308)

`statesync.Handle` runs synchronously inside the sequential event processing loop. Each OpState event performs GetState (1 Redis RT), SetState (1 Redis RT), ProxyPush.SetState (1 HTTP POST), and optionally Registry.MergeLastActive (acquires write lock). A burst of OpState events forces create/delete/update events to wait behind state reconciliation. Consider dispatching OpState handling to a small goroutine worker pool.

---

### Medium: Transient `"resuming"` lock for `AutoResume=false` sandboxes (resumer/resumer.go:115-124)

By moving the `AutoResume` check to inside the `ownErr == nil` branch, sandboxes with `AutoResume=false` briefly acquire the `"resuming"` lock and then immediately `ClearState` it. A concurrent `Sweeper.tryPause` or peer `Resumer` seeing the `"resuming"` marker during this window would skip its decision logic for the TTL duration. The comment block could more explicitly name which concurrent paths are safe and why.

---

### Medium: Synchronous XADD in the user-visible RPC success path (sandbox_update.go:92-96)

The hook fires inline on the success path, doing a synchronous Redis `XADD` before returning the response. The baseline RPC already involves a cross-host Cubelet call; adding another synchronous hop increases tail latency. Errors are swallowed at every layer, so fire-and-forget with a goroutine would be safe here.

---

### Medium: Missing reciprocal mirror annotation on CubeMaster schema types

`CubeMaster/pkg/lifecycle/schema.go` defines `StatePayload` and `SandboxLifecycleMeta` without noting that byte-identical copies exist in `cube-lifecycle-manager/internal/lifecycle/schema.go`. The CLM copy carries the warning; the source of truth should too. Also, the phrase "signals intent" at schema.go:30 is semantically misleading — the event is emitted *after* the RPC succeeds and signals a *completed outcome*, not an intent.

---

### Minor: Duplicated schema files — maintenance burden despite parity_test.go

This PR adds more types/constants to both schema.go files. The existing parity_test.go only validates constant values, not struct field parity. Consider extending it with reflection-based assertions that automatically detect drift in struct fields or JSON tags.

---

### Minor: Bare string literals `"pausing"` / `"resuming"` across three packages

These transition-marker strings appear as literals in `statesync/handler.go`, `resumer/resumer.go`, and `sweeper` (not in this diff). Consider defining them as shared constants in `cube-lifecycle-manager/internal/lifecycle/`.

---

### Test gaps (low-medium severity)

| Gap | File |
|---|---|
| **`statesync.Handle` not tested with `Deps.Registry = nil`** | handler_test.go |
| **No concurrent hook registration stress test** | runtime_ref_hook_test.go |
| **`TestHandle_SetStateErrorStillPushesProxy` doesn't assert `LastActiveMs` is bumped** (would miss a refactor that accidentally gates `MergeLastActive` behind SetState success) | handler_test.go |

---

item.body:
CubeMaster's /cube/sandbox/update handler is stateless — it forwards pause/resume to Cubelet but never tells CLM. When a user manually resumes a paused sandbox via connect(), CLM's Redis state key and CubeProxy's per-worker state dict stay stuck at "paused". The next dataplane request lands on /internal/resume, where CLM's resumer rejects it because auto_resume=False, and the client sees 503 until either the next sweep or a full TTL expiry lets state converge.

This change plumbs a state signal end-to-end:

  * CubeMaster: new OpState event on the existing lifecycle stream, emitted from a new UpdateSandboxSuccessHook after any RetCode==200 pause/resume. Only terminal states ("paused"/"running") are broadcast; transition markers stay private to CLM's SETNX flow. Introducing a hook (instead of calling lifecycle.PublishState directly from sandbox_update.go) keeps the sandbox→lifecycle dependency direction and mirrors the existing create/destroy hooks.

  * CLM: new statesync package consumes OpState events. Reconciles the Redis state key + CubeProxy state dict + registry.LastActiveMs (for running events, so sweeper doesn't immediately re-pause). Skips reconciliation when Redis is at a transition marker (pausing/resuming) so the CLM's own tryPause/doResume can't be clobbered by an external event.

  * Resumer fix: the AutoResume check used to run at the top of doResume, rejecting every request even when Redis already reports "running". After this change it lives inside the ownErr==nil branch — the only path that would call CubeMaster.Resume — so the errAlreadyRunning no-op path lets requests through when the state is already correct (regardless of AutoResume), and a false AutoResume with a still-paused state releases the resuming lock via ClearState so the sweeper isn't stuck for a full TTL.

review_comments.body:
**Synchronous XADD in the RPC success path adds latency**

The hook chain at line 96 fires inline on the success path of a user-visible pause/resume RPC, before the response is returned. `onAfterUpdate` → `PublishState` → `xadd` performs a synchronous Redis `XADD` round-trip. The baseline RPC already involves a cross-host Cubelet call; adding another synchronous hop increases tail latency under Redis I/O contention. Errors are swallowed at every layer, so fire-and-forget (e.g. a goroutine) would be safe here and would not change correctness.

**Transient `"resuming"` lock for `AutoResume=false` sandboxes**

By moving the `AutoResume` check from *before* `acquireResumeOwnership` to *after* it (inside the `ownErr == nil` branch), sandboxes with `AutoResume=false` briefly acquire the `"resuming"` lock (via `acquireResumeOwnership` → `SetState("resuming")`) and then immediately delete it via `ClearState`. A concurrent `Sweeper.tryPause` or peer `Resumer` observing the state key during this window would see `"resuming"` and skip their decision logic for the TTL duration. Under the old code, these sandboxes never touched the state key at all.

Consider extending the comment block (lines 100-108) to explicitly name which concurrent paths see this window and why each is safe, so a future reader doesn't have to trace all callers to validate.

**Bare string literals for transition markers — consider shared constants**

`"pausing"` and `"resuming"` are used as bare string literals here, and also appear in `resumer.go` and `sweeper.go`. They are de facto protocol constants shared by three packages but have no named definition. Consider defining `statePausing` / `stateResuming` as unexported constants in `cube-lifecycle-manager/internal/lifecycle/` (analogous to `StatePaused` / `StateRunning`) so the comparison is compiler-checked rather than copy-paste coordinated.

@@ -0,0 +1,154 @@
+// Copyright (c) 2026 Tencent Inc.
+// SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+//
+
+// Package statesync reconciles the CLM's view of a sandbox's runtime
+// state with pause / resume actions driven externally through CubeMaster.
+//
+// CubeMaster is a stateless proxy: when the SDK calls Sandbox.connect() to
+// resume a paused sandbox, CubeMaster forwards the RPC to Cubelet but does
+// not touch the CLM's state key or CubeProxy's per-worker state dict.
+// Without a nudge from CubeMaster the CLM would keep thinking the
+// sandbox is paused and reject the next request from the dataplane.
+//
+// CubeMaster now emits an OpState event on the lifecycle events stream after
+// every successful pause / resume RPC (see CubeMaster/pkg/lifecycle/store.go
+// PublishState). This package consumes those events and reconciles:
+//
+//   - Redis state key (cube:v1:shared:sandbox:lifecycle:state:<id>)
+//   - CubeProxy's cube_sandbox_state dict (via proxypush.SetState)
+//   - registry.Entry.LastActiveMs when the new state is "running"
+//     (mirrors resumer.doResume: avoids the sweeper re-pausing a sandbox
+//     that just came back).
+//
+// The event source (CubeMaster) is stateless with respect to the CLM's
+// SETNX-based transition locks ("pausing", "resuming"). To avoid a state
+// event racing an in-flight sweeper.tryPause or resumer.doResume, Handle
+// skips reconciliation whenever the current state key holds a transition
+// marker; the CLM's own flow will write the terminal state moments
+// later, so the event is redundant.
+package statesync
+
+import (
+	"context"
+	"time"
+
+	"go.uber.org/zap"
+
+	"github.com/tencentcloud/CubeSandbox/cube-lifecycle-manager/internal/lifecycle"
+	"github.com/tencentcloud/CubeSandbox/cube-lifecycle-manager/internal/redisstream"
+	"github.com/tencentcloud/CubeSandbox/cube-lifecycle-manager/internal/registry"
+)
+
+// Deps bundles the dependencies a Handle call needs. Constructed once at
+// startup in main.go and reused for every event.
+type Deps struct {
+	Registry  *registry.Registry
+	Redis     stateStore
+	ProxyPush stateNotifier
+	// TTL is the state key TTL applied when we SET the new state. Uses the
+	// same value as sweeper/resumer's StateLockTTL so a state written from
+	// this path is indistinguishable from one written by the CLM itself.
+	TTL time.Duration
+	Log *zap.Logger
+	// Now returns the current time. Injectable for tests.
+	Now func() time.Time
+}
+
+// Handle applies a single OpState event. It is intentionally best-effort:
+// partial failures are logged and swallowed so a Redis blip cannot poison
+// the stream consumer loop.
+func Handle(ctx context.Context, d Deps, ev redisstream.Event) {
+	log := d.Log
+	if log == nil {
+		log = zap.NewNop()
+	}
+	now := d.Now
+	if now == nil {
+		now = time.Now
+	}
+
+	if ev.SandboxID == "" {
+		log.Warn("state event missing sandbox id")
+		return
+	}
+	if ev.State == nil {
+		log.Warn("state event missing payload",
+			zap.String("sandbox_id", ev.SandboxID),
+			zap.String("stream_id", ev.StreamID))
+		return
+	}
+
+	newState := ev.State.State
+	if newState != lifecycle.StatePaused && newState != lifecycle.StateRunning {
+		log.Warn("state event has invalid state",
+			zap.String("sandbox_id", ev.SandboxID),
+			zap.String("state", newState))
+		return
+	}
+
+	if d.Registry == nil || d.Registry.Get(ev.SandboxID) == nil {
+		// Sandbox is not (yet) known to the CLM. This can happen when
+		// the state event overtakes its own create event (unlikely — same
+		// stream, same partition — but cheap to guard). Ignore: the create
+		// event will populate the registry and any subsequent state
+		// reconciliation will pick things up.
+		log.Warn("state event for unknown sandbox",
+			zap.String("sandbox_id", ev.SandboxID),
+			zap.String("state", newState))
+		return
+	}
+

**TOCTOU race: non-atomic read-check-write against the Redis state key**

`GetState` on line 102 reads the current state, lines 114-120 check for transition markers, and line 127 writes the new terminal state via `SetState`. Because none of these operations are atomic, the CLM's sweeper or resumer could SETNX a transition marker (`"pausing"`/`"resuming"`) between the read (102) and the write (127). `SetState` unconditionally overwrites, destroying the transition lock mid-flight.

This can silently abort an in-progress auto-pause (a `"running"` event from an external resume overwrites a `"pausing"` lock) or strand a dataplane request (a `"paused"` event overwrites a `"resuming"` lock).

Consider using a Lua script that atomically GET-and-SET only when the current value is a terminal state, rather than relying on read-check-write with the transition-marker guard.

## Code Review: PR #955 — feat(CubeProxy): make admin port configurable and detect port conflicts

### Overview

Well-structured PR that consistently parameterizes the admin port across six deployment paths (one-click shell, systemd postcheck, Terraform, build-bundle, tests, docs). The fail-fast port conflict detection is the right approach. A few noteworthy issues below.

---

### Finding 1 (Medium): Admin listen address widened from loopback, auth token defaults to empty

The admin listen address was previously hard-coded to 127.0.0.1:8082 (loopback-only). The one-click path now defaults CUBE_PROXY_ADMIN_LISTEN to CUBE_SANDBOX_NODE_IP (cluster-reachable), and the Terraform/K8s path hard-codes 0.0.0.0. Meanwhile, CUBE_ADMIN_TOKEN defaults to empty in the one-click path.

The admin endpoints (POST /admin/meta/delete, POST /admin/state, etc.) are now reachable from the network in a default deployment with no auth barrier. On a multi-node cluster, any host that can reach the proxy's node IP could interfere with sandbox lifecycle management.

**Locations**: up-cube-proxy.sh:43, up-cube-proxy.sh:63, tke-addons.tf:116

**Suggestion**: Auto-generate a random admin token when the listen address is not 127.0.0.1, or emit a loud warning when CUBE_PROXY_ADMIN_LISTEN is non-loopback and CUBE_ADMIN_TOKEN is empty.

---

### Finding 2 (Medium): Port-conflict error message always suggests admin-port override

up-cube-proxy.sh:191 — The die() message unconditionally appends the admin-port override hint regardless of which port conflicted. When port 80 (HTTP) is the conflict, suggesting CUBE_PROXY_ADMIN_PORT override is misleading. The hint should only appear for the admin port.

---

### Finding 3 (Medium): Missing port-range validation in shell script path

Terraform validates cube_proxy_admin_port (1-65535) via HCL (variables.tf:436), but up-cube-proxy.sh:47 accepts any string. A non-numeric value would cause ss to fail silently (treated as "not in use") and nginx to bind to whatever the value parses as. Adding a validation guard would give operators immediate feedback.

---

### Finding 4 (Low): Test coverage gaps

All five test_cube_proxy_postcheck_* callers leave admin_port at the default 8082 — the headline feature (port configurability) has no test coverage in the postcheck path. The pre-flight port conflict detection logic (up-cube-proxy.sh:189-193) also has zero test coverage.

---

### Positive notes

- Consistent template changes across all four rendering paths with matching fallback validation loops
- Useful error messages pointing operators to docker logs and CUBE_PROXY_ADMIN_PORT
- Admin port now participates in both Docker readiness and systemd postcheck gating
- dump_failed_cube_units in install.sh catches silent Wants= dependency failures
- Terraform containerPort and env-var wiring correctly updated

item.body:
## Summary
CubeProxy runs with host networking and hard-coded its admin server to `8082`. When another process already holds that port, nginx dies with `bind() to <node-ip>:8082 failed (98: Address in use)` and the container crash-loops — while the one-click installer silently stalls at `systemctl enable --now cube-sandbox-control.target`, never surfacing the real cause.

This PR makes the admin port configurable via **`CUBE_PROXY_ADMIN_PORT`** (default `8082`, fully backward-compatible) and adds fail-fast conflict detection so the failure is caught early with a clear message.

Closes #945


### Root cause
Two independent defects:

1. **Admin port not configurable.** A prior change parametrized the admin *listen address* (`CUBE_PROXY_ADMIN_LISTEN`) but left the *port* `8082` hard-coded in the nginx template transforms, `CUBE_PROXY_ID` / `CUBE_PROXY_ADMIN_URL`, and the Terraform/K8s deployment — unlike HTTP/HTTPS which already have `CUBE_PROXY_HTTP_PORT` / `CUBE_PROXY_HTTPS_PORT`.

2. **Silent failure.** The pre-start conflict check only covered HTTP/HTTPS, and both the post-start readiness loop and the systemd post-start check only waited on the HTTP port — so an admin-bind failure (which kills the whole nginx master) went undetected and the installer just hung.

  ### Changes
  
**One-click / systemd path**
- `up-cube-proxy.sh`: new `CUBE_PROXY_ADMIN_PORT`; renders the new template placeholder; derives `CUBE_PROXY_ID` / `CUBE_PROXY_ADMIN_URL` from it; adds the admin port to the pre-start conflict check and the post-start readiness loop (distinct error naming the admin port + `docker logs` hint). surfaces here instead of stalling `cube-sandbox-control.target`.
- `env.example`: documents the new variable.
  
**nginx templating**
- `build-release-bundle.sh`, `tests/test_package_layout.sh`, `terraform/tencentcloud/create.sh`: sed transforms now emit `__CUBE_PROXY_ADMIN_LISTEN__:__CUBE_PROXY_ADMIN_PORT__` and the placeholder-validation loops include the new token.

**Terraform / K8s**
- `variables.tf`: new validated `cube_proxy_admin_port` (default 8082).
- `tke-addons.tf`: substitutes the port placeholder, updates the inline fallback, `containerPort`, and the `CUBE_PROXY_ADMIN_URL` / `CUBE_PROXY_RESUME_URL` env values.

**Docs**
- `docs/guide/lifecycle.md`, `docs/zh/guide/lifecycle.md`.

review_comments.body:
**Missing input validation for CUBE_PROXY_ADMIN_PORT**

The Terraform variable `cube_proxy_admin_port` has type + range validation (`> 0 && < 65536`). The shell-script path has none — if someone exports `CUBE_PROXY_ADMIN_PORT=abc` or an empty string, it's passed directly into `ss` (producing a confusing error or silently matching all ports) and `escape_sed`.

Add a validation guard after the default assignment, similar to what `COMPOSE_DETACH` does on line 87-90:

```bash
CUBE_PROXY_ADMIN_PORT="${CUBE_PROXY_ADMIN_PORT:-8082}"
[[ "${CUBE_PROXY_ADMIN_PORT}" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] \
  && (( CUBE_PROXY_ADMIN_PORT >= 1 && CUBE_PROXY_ADMIN_PORT <= 65535 )) \
  || die "CUBE_PROXY_ADMIN_PORT must be a valid TCP port (1-65535), got: ${CUBE_PROXY_ADMIN_PORT}"
```

(Same guard could apply to `CUBE_PROXY_HTTP_PORT` and `CUBE_PROXY_HTTPS_PORT` too, though that's pre-existing.)

## Review: PR #952 — Docs/Integrations: Add LangChain Integration Guide

**Overall:** A well-structured, comprehensive guide with clean Python code, thorough bilingual documentation, and thoughtful attention to edge cases. The PR is in strong shape — no critical bugs or security vulnerabilities. Below is feedback worth addressing before merge.

---

### High Impact

1. **`docs/guide/integrations/langchain.md:79` — Dockerfile snippet omits version pins**
   The actual `Dockerfile` pins `pandas==2.2.3`, `numpy==1.26.4`, `matplotlib==3.9.3`, `scikit-learn==1.6.1` for reproducible builds, but the doc snippet shows unpinned packages. Readers who copy the snippet lose reproducibility. Update the doc snippet to match the real file. Same fix needed in `docs/zh/guide/integrations/langchain.md:76`.

2. **`docs/guide/integrations/langchain.md:190` — API key resolution diverges from actual code**
   The doc excerpt for `ChatOpenAI` re-computes `api_key` inline, while the actual `langchain_agent_demo.py:56` resolves it once at module scope and validates it via `sys.exit(1)`. Users copying only the excerpt lose the early-exit guard for missing keys. Align the excerpt with the real `build_agent()` function. Same fix in `docs/zh/guide/integrations/langchain.md:187`.

---

### Medium Impact

3. **`examples/langchain-integration/.env.example:12` — Misleading E2B_API_KEY placeholder**
   `<your-e2b-api-key>` looks like a real credential is required. Align with `pi-agent-integration/.env.example` which says "any non-empty value in local dev; a real key when auth is enabled". Suggestion: `E2B_API_KEY="e2b_local_dev"` with an explanatory comment.

4. **`examples/langchain-integration/langchain_agent_demo.py:38` — SSL_CERT_FILE override is process-wide**
   Setting `os.environ["SSL_CERT_FILE"]` affects ALL HTTPS connections, including LLM API calls. If the custom CA doesn't include public root CAs, LLM TLS will fail. Either scope the override to CubeAPI only, or add a doc warning.

5. **`examples/langchain-integration/Dockerfile:11` — Unnecessary packages add ~40-60 MB**
   `python3-venv` and `git` are installed but never used in the example. Removing them shrinks pull time and storage.

---

### Low Impact / Polish

6. **`examples/langchain-integration/langchain_agent_demo.py:119`** — `build_agent()` closes over module-level `_api_key`, making it untestable. Consider passing it as a parameter.

7. **Placeholder format inconsistency**: `.env.example` uses `<your-cube-sandbox-ip>` while docs and READMEs use `<your-cube-host>` / `<node>`. Pick one.

8. **Docs Caveats wording**: "after all imports" (langchain.md Caveats) is slightly imprecise — the `default_username` assignment is placed after utility imports but *before* `from e2b import Sandbox`. Minor, but the doc code snippet itself is correct.

---

### Test Coverage

The example directory has no tests, unlike several other examples in the repo (e.g., `e2b-dev-sidecar/`, `cubesandbox-base-nginx/`). Key untested paths:
- Four output branches of `run_python` (stdout, stderr, both, neither × exit code)
- Cleanup safety on `Sandbox.create()` failure and `kill()` failure
- All three `sys.exit(1)` env validation paths

Consider adding a `test_langchain_demo.py` following the patterns in `test_dev_sidecar.py`.

---

### Security

No critical or high-severity issues found. The architecture is sound: agent-generated code runs inside KVM MicroVMs, the "Going Further" section correctly demonstrates default-deny egress with on-the-wire key injection, and no hardcoded credentials exist.

---

### Positive Highlights

- Robust cleanup pattern with nested try/except (line 109-114)
- Early envd user configuration before Filesystem construction
- Thorough Caveats section documenting known tradeoffs
- Faithful English/Chinese translation parity
- `.gitignore` correctly excludes `.env` while keeping `.env.example`
- Pinned Docker versions for reproducible builds in the actual file
<!-- cubesandbox-auto-review:end -->

+---
+title: LangChain Integration Guide
+author: peerless-hero
+date: 2026-07-07
+tags:
+  - integration
+  - langchain
+  - agent
+lang: en-US
+---
+
+# LangChain Integration Guide
+
+[中文文档](../../zh/guide/integrations/langchain.md)
+
+Run a [LangChain](https://github.com/langchain-ai/langchain) agent — whose tools execute
+Python — inside [CubeSandbox](https://github.com/TencentCloud/CubeSandbox) MicroVMs. Because
+Cube exposes an **E2B-compatible API**, moving a LangChain app from E2B to Cube is usually a
+single environment-variable change, while gaining KVM-level isolation for every line of
+agent-generated code. This guide ships with a runnable
+[`examples/langchain-integration`](https://github.com/TencentCloud/CubeSandbox/tree/master/examples/langchain-integration)
+project.
+
+## Integration Target and Version
+
+| Component | Version |
+|---|---|
+| LangChain | `langchain` `>= 0.3` |
+| langchain-openai | `>= 0.2` |
+| LangGraph (prebuilt ReAct agent) | `langgraph` `>= 0.2` |
+| E2B SDK (E2B-compatible driver) | `e2b` (latest) |
+| CubeSandbox base image | `ghcr.io/tencentcloud/cubesandbox-base:2026.16` |
+| CubeSandbox platform | `>= 0.3.0` |
+
+## Prerequisites
+
+- A running CubeSandbox deployment; CubeAPI reachable at `http://<node>:3000`.
+- `cubemastercli` on `$PATH`, connected to the cluster.
+- Docker on the build workstation, plus a registry the Cube nodes can pull from.
+- An OpenAI-compatible LLM endpoint (TokenHub is used in the example; any
+  OpenAI-compatible endpoint works via `OPENAI_BASE_URL` / `OPENAI_API_KEY`).
+- Python 3.10+ for the host driver scripts.
+
+## Why Run LangChain Agents Inside a Sandbox
+
+LangChain agents frequently expose a code-execution tool (data analysis, file transforms,
+shelling out). Running that tool on the host blends the agent's blast radius with your dev
+machine. Running it inside CubeSandbox gives you:
+
+| Concern | CubeSandbox provides |
+|---|---|
+| **Isolation** | KVM MicroVM per session, dedicated guest kernel — agent code cannot touch the host |
+| **Reproducibility** | Every session boots from the same template snapshot |
+| **Fast spin-up** | Sub-60 ms cold start, so many parallel agents are cheap |
+| **Long tasks** | `sandbox.pause()` snapshots VM + rootfs; resume later |
+| **Key hygiene** | CubeEgress can inject the LLM auth header on the wire — the VM never sees the real key |
+| **Egress audit** | Every outbound request is recorded in the egress audit log |
+
+## Integration Steps
+
+### 1. Build the template image
+
+The image stacks a Python data-science stack on top of `cubesandbox-base` (envd already
+listens on `:49983`).
+
+```dockerfile
+# examples/langchain-integration/Dockerfile
+ARG CUBE_BASE_IMAGE=ghcr.io/tencentcloud/cubesandbox-base:2026.16
+FROM ${CUBE_BASE_IMAGE}
+
+ARG DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive
+
+RUN apt-get update \
+    && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
+        python3 python3-pip python3-venv ca-certificates git \
+    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*
+
+# Pin data-science versions for reproducible builds. Bump as needed.
+RUN python3 -m pip install --no-cache-dir --break-system-packages \
+        pandas==2.2.3 numpy==1.26.4 matplotlib==3.9.3 scikit-learn==1.6.1
+
+WORKDIR /workspace
+
+# Pre-seed a demo dataset so the example agent can run without external inputs.
+COPY sales.csv /workspace/sales.csv
+
+EXPOSE 49983
+```
+
+Build and push:
+
+```bash
+docker build --platform linux/amd64 \
+  -t <your-registry>/langchain-cube:latest \
+  examples/langchain-integration
+docker push <your-registry>/langchain-cube:latest
+```
+
+### 2. Register as a Cube template
+
+```bash
+cubemastercli tpl create-from-image \
+  --image <your-registry>/langchain-cube:latest \
+  --writable-layer-size 2G \
+  --expose-port 49983 \
+  --probe       49983 \
+  --probe-path  /health
+
+cubemastercli tpl watch --job-id <job_id>
+```
+
+Once the job reaches `READY`, note the `template_id` — you pass it to every
+`Sandbox.create()` call. `2G` writable layer suits medium analysis tasks; bump to `4G+`
+if the agent installs large packages at runtime.
+
+### 3. Install dependencies and configure env
+
+```bash
+cd examples/langchain-integration
+cp .env.example .env
+# fill in E2B_API_URL (CubeAPI), E2B_API_KEY, CUBE_TEMPLATE_ID, and your LLM key
+pip install -r requirements.txt
+```
+
+| Variable | Where it flows | Notes |
+|---|---|---|
+| `E2B_API_URL` | Local process | CubeAPI address (`http://<node>:3000`) |
+| `E2B_API_KEY` | Local process | Any non-empty string in local dev |
+| `CUBE_TEMPLATE_ID` | `Sandbox.create(template=...)` | From step 2 |
+| `OPENAI_API_KEY` / `TOKENHUB_API_KEY` | LLM client | OpenAI-compatible key |
+| `OPENAI_BASE_URL` | LLM client | e.g. `https://tokenhub.tencentmaas.com/v1` |
+| `CHAT_MODEL` | LLM client | e.g. `deepseek-v3` |
+| `CUBE_SSL_CERT_FILE` | Local process | Optional CA bundle for HTTPS CubeAPI |
+
+### 4. Wire the code-execution tool to Cube
+
+The agent is unchanged; only the tool body swaps from a local REPL to a Cube Sandbox.
+
+```python
+# langchain_agent_demo.py (excerpt — env validation and tool definition)
+import os
+from dotenv import load_dotenv
+
+load_dotenv()
+# After load_dotenv, the script validates CUBE_TEMPLATE_ID, E2B_API_KEY,
+# and the LLM API key, then:
+import e2b.envd.rpc as _e2b_rpc
+_e2b_rpc.default_username = "root"   # Cube's envd serves only root
+
+from e2b import Sandbox                       # E2B-compatible; talks to CubeAPI
+from langchain_core.tools import tool
+
+
+@tool
+def run_python(code: str) -> str:
+    """Execute Python inside a Cube Sandbox MicroVM and return stdout/stderr."""
+    sandbox = None
+    try:
+        sandbox = Sandbox.create(
+            template=os.environ["CUBE_TEMPLATE_ID"], timeout=300
+        )
+        sandbox.files.write("/workspace/_agent_code.py", code)
+        res = sandbox.commands.run(
+            "python3 /workspace/_agent_code.py", user="root", timeout=120
+        )
+        out: list[str] = []
+        if res.stdout:
+            out.append(res.stdout)
+        if res.stderr:
+            out.append("stderr:\n" + res.stderr)
+        if not out:
+            out.append(f"(exit code {res.exit_code})" if res.exit_code != 0 else "(no output)")
+        return "\n".join(out)
+    finally:
+        if sandbox is not None:
+            try:
+                sandbox.kill()
+            except Exception:
+                pass  # cleanup failure must not mask the original exception

+KVM MicroVM, so the host is never touched by agent-generated code.
+
+What it shows
+-------------
+- A Cube (E2B-compatible) `Sandbox` used as the execution backend for a
+  LangChain tool.
+- A ReAct agent built with LangGraph's `create_react_agent`.
+- The near-zero-refactor story: point `E2B_API_URL` at CubeAPI and the existing
+  E2B code path works unchanged.
+
+Usage
+-----
+    cp .env.example .env   # fill in real values
+    pip install -r requirements.txt
+    python langchain_agent_demo.py
+    python langchain_agent_demo.py --question "Train a linear model and report RMSE."
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import argparse
+import os
+import sys
+import traceback
+
+from dotenv import load_dotenv
+
+load_dotenv()
+
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# CUBE_SSL_CERT_FILE → SSL_CERT_FILE (for HTTPS CubeAPI deployments)
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+_cube_ssl = os.environ.get("CUBE_SSL_CERT_FILE")
+if _cube_ssl and os.path.isfile(_cube_ssl):
+    os.environ["SSL_CERT_FILE"] = _cube_ssl
+
+# Warn when running over plain HTTP (sandbox traffic in cleartext)
+_e2b_api_url = os.environ.get("E2B_API_URL", "")
+if _e2b_api_url.startswith("http://"):
+    print(
+        "Warning: E2B_API_URL uses plain HTTP — sandbox traffic (code, keys, data) "
+        "is transmitted in cleartext.",
+        file=sys.stderr,
+    )
+
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Environment variable validation — fail fast with clear messages
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+_REQUIRED_ENV = {
+    "CUBE_TEMPLATE_ID": "set CUBE_TEMPLATE_ID=<template-id> in .env",
+    "E2B_API_KEY": "set E2B_API_KEY=<any-non-empty-string> in .env",
+}
+_UNSET = []
+for var, hint in _REQUIRED_ENV.items():
+    if not os.environ.get(var):
+        _UNSET.append(f"  {var} — {hint}")
+if _UNSET:
+    print("Missing required environment variables:", file=sys.stderr)
+    print("\n".join(_UNSET), file=sys.stderr)
+    sys.exit(1)
+
+_api_key = os.getenv("OPENAI_API_KEY") or os.getenv("TOKENHUB_API_KEY")
+if not _api_key:
+    print(
+        "Missing LLM API key. Set either OPENAI_API_KEY or TOKENHUB_API_KEY in .env",
+        file=sys.stderr,
+    )
+    sys.exit(1)
+
+import e2b.envd.rpc as _e2b_rpc

+---
+title: LangChain 集成指南
+author: peerless-hero
+date: 2026-07-07
+tags:
+  - integration
+  - langchain
+  - agent
+lang: zh-CN
+---
+
+# LangChain 集成指南
+
+[English](../../guide/integrations/langchain.md)
+
+将调用 Python 工具的 [LangChain](https://github.com/langchain-ai/langchain) Agent 运行在
+[CubeSandbox](https://github.com/TencentCloud/CubeSandbox) 的 MicroVM 中。由于 Cube 暴露了
+**与 E2B 兼容的 API**，把 LangChain 应用从 E2B 迁移到 Cube 通常只需改一个环境变量，同时还能为
+Agent 生成的每一行代码获得 KVM 级隔离。本文附带可运行的
+[`examples/langchain-integration`](https://github.com/TencentCloud/CubeSandbox/tree/master/examples/langchain-integration)
+示例工程。
+
+## 集成对象与版本
+
+| 组件 | 版本 |
+|---|---|
+| LangChain | `langchain` `>= 0.3` |
+| langchain-openai | `>= 0.2` |
+| LangGraph（预置 ReAct Agent） | `langgraph` `>= 0.2` |
+| E2B SDK（E2B 兼容驱动） | `e2b`（最新） |
+| CubeSandbox 基础镜像 | `ghcr.io/tencentcloud/cubesandbox-base:2026.16` |
+| CubeSandbox 平台 | `>= 0.3.0` |
+
+## 前置条件
+
+- 已部署 CubeSandbox，CubeAPI 可从 `http://<node>:3000` 访问。
+- `$PATH` 中包含 `cubemastercli`，并已连接到集群。
+- 构建工作站已安装 Docker，且 Cube 节点可拉取的镜像仓库。
+- 一个 OpenAI 兼容的 LLM 端点（示例使用 TokenHub；任何 OpenAI 兼容端点均可经
+  `OPENAI_BASE_URL` / `OPENAI_API_KEY` 接入）。
+- 主机驱动脚本需要 Python 3.10+。
+
+## 为什么把 LangChain Agent 放进沙箱
+
+LangChain Agent 经常会暴露代码执行工具（数据分析、文件转换、调用 shell）。在宿主机上运行该工具，
+会把 Agent 的影响范围与你的开发机混在一起。放进 CubeSandbox 后，你将获得：
+
+| 关注点 | CubeSandbox 提供 |
+|---|---|
+| **隔离** | 每个会话一个 KVM MicroVM，独立客户机内核——Agent 代码无法触碰宿主机 |
+| **可复现** | 每次会话都从同一个模板快照启动 |
+| **快速启动** | 冷启动低于 60ms，因此并行跑多个 Agent 成本很低 |
+| **长任务** | `sandbox.pause()` 快照 VM + 根文件系统，稍后恢复 |
+| **密钥卫生** | CubeEgress 可在网络层注入 LLM 鉴权头——VM 内永远看不到真实密钥 |
+| **出口审计** | 每一次出站请求都会记录到出口审计日志 |
+
+## 接入步骤
+
+### 1. 构建模板镜像
+
+在 `cubesandbox-base` 之上叠加 Python 数据科学栈（envd 已在 `:49983` 监听）。
+
+```dockerfile
+# examples/langchain-integration/Dockerfile
+ARG CUBE_BASE_IMAGE=ghcr.io/tencentcloud/cubesandbox-base:2026.16
+FROM ${CUBE_BASE_IMAGE}
+
+ARG DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive
+
+RUN apt-get update \
+    && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
+        python3 python3-pip python3-venv ca-certificates git \
+    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*
+
+# 为可复现构建锁定版本，按需升级
+RUN python3 -m pip install --no-cache-dir --break-system-packages \
+        pandas==2.2.3 numpy==1.26.4 matplotlib==3.9.3 scikit-learn==1.6.1
+
+WORKDIR /workspace
+
+# 预置演示数据集，使示例 Agent 无需外部输入即可运行
+COPY sales.csv /workspace/sales.csv
+
+EXPOSE 49983
+```
+
+构建并推送：
+
+```bash
+docker build --platform linux/amd64 \
+  -t <your-registry>/langchain-cube:latest \
+  examples/langchain-integration
+docker push <your-registry>/langchain-cube:latest
+```
+
+### 2. 注册为 Cube 模板
+
+```bash
+cubemastercli tpl create-from-image \
+  --image <your-registry>/langchain-cube:latest \
+  --writable-layer-size 2G \
+  --expose-port 49983 \
+  --probe       49983 \
+  --probe-path  /health
+
+cubemastercli tpl watch --job-id <job_id>
+```
+
+任务进入 `READY` 后，记下 `template_id`——每次 `Sandbox.create()` 都要传入它。`2G` 可写层适合中等
+分析任务；若 Agent 运行时安装大体积包，可调到 `4G+`。
+
+### 3. 安装依赖并配置环境变量
+
+```bash
+cd examples/langchain-integration
+cp .env.example .env
+# 填写 E2B_API_URL（CubeAPI）、E2B_API_KEY、CUBE_TEMPLATE_ID 以及你的 LLM 密钥
+pip install -r requirements.txt
+```
+
+| 变量 | 流向 | 说明 |
+|---|---|---|
+| `E2B_API_URL` | 本地进程 | CubeAPI 地址（`http://<node>:3000`） |
+| `E2B_API_KEY` | 本地进程 | 本地开发填任意非空字符串 |
+| `CUBE_TEMPLATE_ID` | `Sandbox.create(template=...)` | 来自步骤 2 |
+| `OPENAI_API_KEY` / `TOKENHUB_API_KEY` | LLM 客户端 | OpenAI 兼容密钥 |
+| `OPENAI_BASE_URL` | LLM 客户端 | 如 `https://tokenhub.tencentmaas.com/v1` |
+| `CHAT_MODEL` | LLM 客户端 | 如 `deepseek-v3` |
+| `CUBE_SSL_CERT_FILE` | 本地进程 | （可选）HTTPS CubeAPI 的 CA 证书路径 |
+
+### 4. 把代码执行工具接到 Cube
+
+Agent 本身不变，只是工具体从本地 REPL 换成 Cube 沙箱。
+
+```python
+# langchain_agent_demo.py（节选——环境变量校验与工具定义）
+import os
+from dotenv import load_dotenv
+
+load_dotenv()
+# load_dotenv 后，脚本会校验 CUBE_TEMPLATE_ID、E2B_API_KEY、LLM API key，
+# 然后：
+import e2b.envd.rpc as _e2b_rpc
+_e2b_rpc.default_username = "root"   # Cube 的 envd 只服务 root
+
+from e2b import Sandbox                       # E2B 兼容；连接 CubeAPI
+from langchain_core.tools import tool
+
+
+@tool
+def run_python(code: str) -> str:
+    """在 Cube Sandbox MicroVM 内执行 Python，并返回 stdout/stderr。"""
+    sandbox = None
+    try:
+        sandbox = Sandbox.create(
+            template=os.environ["CUBE_TEMPLATE_ID"], timeout=300
+        )
+        sandbox.files.write("/workspace/_agent_code.py", code)
+        res = sandbox.commands.run(
+            "python3 /workspace/_agent_code.py", user="root", timeout=120
+        )
+        out: list[str] = []
+        if res.stdout:
+            out.append(res.stdout)
+        if res.stderr:
+            out.append("stderr:\n" + res.stderr)
+        if not out:
+            out.append(f"(exit code {res.exit_code})" if res.exit_code != 0 else "(无输出)")
+        return "\n".join(out)
+    finally:
+        if sandbox is not None:
+            try:
+                sandbox.kill()
+            except Exception:
+                pass  # 清理失败不能掩盖原始异常
+```
+
+### 5. 运行 Agent
+
+```python
+from langchain_openai import ChatOpenAI
+from langchain_core.messages import HumanMessage
+from langgraph.prebuilt import create_react_agent
+
+llm = ChatOpenAI(
+    model=os.getenv("CHAT_MODEL", "deepseek-v3"),
+    api_key=os.getenv("OPENAI_API_KEY") or os.getenv("TOKENHUB_API_KEY"),
+    base_url=os.getenv("OPENAI_BASE_URL", "https://tokenhub.tencentmaas.com/v1"),
+    temperature=0,
+)

+---
+
+# LangChain Integration Guide
+
+[中文文档](../../zh/guide/integrations/langchain.md)
+
+Run a [LangChain](https://github.com/langchain-ai/langchain) agent — whose tools execute
+Python — inside [CubeSandbox](https://github.com/TencentCloud/CubeSandbox) MicroVMs. Because
+Cube exposes an **E2B-compatible API**, moving a LangChain app from E2B to Cube is usually a
+single environment-variable change, while gaining KVM-level isolation for every line of
+agent-generated code. This guide ships with a runnable
+[`examples/langchain-integration`](https://github.com/TencentCloud/CubeSandbox/tree/master/examples/langchain-integration)
+project.
+
+## Integration Target and Version
+
+| Component | Version |
+|---|---|
+| LangChain | `langchain` `>= 0.3` |
+| langchain-openai | `>= 0.2` |
+| LangGraph (prebuilt ReAct agent) | `langgraph` `>= 0.2` |
+| E2B SDK (E2B-compatible driver) | `e2b` (latest) |
+| CubeSandbox base image | `ghcr.io/tencentcloud/cubesandbox-base:2026.16` |
+| CubeSandbox platform | `>= 0.3.0` |
+
+## Prerequisites
+
+- A running CubeSandbox deployment; CubeAPI reachable at `http://<node>:3000`.
+- `cubemastercli` on `$PATH`, connected to the cluster.
+- Docker on the build workstation, plus a registry the Cube nodes can pull from.
+- An OpenAI-compatible LLM endpoint (TokenHub is used in the example; any
+  OpenAI-compatible endpoint works via `OPENAI_BASE_URL` / `OPENAI_API_KEY`).
+- Python 3.10+ for the host driver scripts.
+
+## Why Run LangChain Agents Inside a Sandbox
+
+LangChain agents frequently expose a code-execution tool (data analysis, file transforms,
+shelling out). Running that tool on the host blends the agent's blast radius with your dev
+machine. Running it inside CubeSandbox gives you:
+
+| Concern | CubeSandbox provides |
+|---|---|
+| **Isolation** | KVM MicroVM per session, dedicated guest kernel — agent code cannot touch the host |
+| **Reproducibility** | Every session boots from the same template snapshot |
+| **Fast spin-up** | Sub-60 ms cold start, so many parallel agents are cheap |
+| **Long tasks** | `sandbox.pause()` snapshots VM + rootfs; resume later |
+| **Key hygiene** | CubeEgress can inject the LLM auth header on the wire — the VM never sees the real key |
+| **Egress audit** | Every outbound request is recorded in the egress audit log |
+
+## Integration Steps
+
+### 1. Build the template image
+
+The image stacks a Python data-science stack on top of `cubesandbox-base` (envd already
+listens on `:49983`).
+
+```dockerfile
+# examples/langchain-integration/Dockerfile
+ARG CUBE_BASE_IMAGE=ghcr.io/tencentcloud/cubesandbox-base:2026.16
+FROM ${CUBE_BASE_IMAGE}
+
+ARG DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive
+
+RUN apt-get update \
+    && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
+        python3 python3-pip python3-venv ca-certificates git \
+    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*
+
+# Pin data-science versions for reproducible builds. Bump as needed.
+RUN python3 -m pip install --no-cache-dir --break-system-packages \
+        pandas==2.2.3 numpy==1.26.4 matplotlib==3.9.3 scikit-learn==1.6.1
+
+WORKDIR /workspace
+
+# Pre-seed a demo dataset so the example agent can run without external inputs.
+COPY sales.csv /workspace/sales.csv
+
+EXPOSE 49983
+```
+
+Build and push:
+
+```bash
+docker build --platform linux/amd64 \
+  -t <your-registry>/langchain-cube:latest \
+  examples/langchain-integration
+docker push <your-registry>/langchain-cube:latest
+```
+
+### 2. Register as a Cube template
+
+```bash
+cubemastercli tpl create-from-image \
+  --image <your-registry>/langchain-cube:latest \
+  --writable-layer-size 2G \
+  --expose-port 49983 \
+  --probe       49983 \
+  --probe-path  /health
+
+cubemastercli tpl watch --job-id <job_id>
+```
+
+Once the job reaches `READY`, note the `template_id` — you pass it to every
+`Sandbox.create()` call. `2G` writable layer suits medium analysis tasks; bump to `4G+`
+if the agent installs large packages at runtime.
+
+### 3. Install dependencies and configure env
+
+```bash
+cd examples/langchain-integration
+cp .env.example .env
+# fill in E2B_API_URL (CubeAPI), E2B_API_KEY, CUBE_TEMPLATE_ID, and your LLM key
+pip install -r requirements.txt
+```
+
+| Variable | Where it flows | Notes |
+|---|---|---|
+| `E2B_API_URL` | Local process | CubeAPI address (`http://<node>:3000`) |
+| `E2B_API_KEY` | Local process | Any non-empty string in local dev |
+| `CUBE_TEMPLATE_ID` | `Sandbox.create(template=...)` | From step 2 |
+| `OPENAI_API_KEY` / `TOKENHUB_API_KEY` | LLM client | OpenAI-compatible key |
+| `OPENAI_BASE_URL` | LLM client | e.g. `https://tokenhub.tencentmaas.com/v1` |
+| `CHAT_MODEL` | LLM client | e.g. `deepseek-v3` |
+| `CUBE_SSL_CERT_FILE` | Local process | Optional CA bundle for HTTPS CubeAPI |
+
+### 4. Wire the code-execution tool to Cube
+
+The agent is unchanged; only the tool body swaps from a local REPL to a Cube Sandbox.
+
+```python
+# langchain_agent_demo.py (excerpt — env validation and tool definition)
+import os
+from dotenv import load_dotenv
+
+load_dotenv()
+# After load_dotenv, the script validates CUBE_TEMPLATE_ID, E2B_API_KEY,
+# and the LLM API key, then:
+import e2b.envd.rpc as _e2b_rpc
+_e2b_rpc.default_username = "root"   # Cube's envd serves only root
+
+from e2b import Sandbox                       # E2B-compatible; talks to CubeAPI
+from langchain_core.tools import tool
+
+
+@tool
+def run_python(code: str) -> str:
+    """Execute Python inside a Cube Sandbox MicroVM and return stdout/stderr."""
+    sandbox = None
+    try:
+        sandbox = Sandbox.create(
+            template=os.environ["CUBE_TEMPLATE_ID"], timeout=300
+        )
+        sandbox.files.write("/workspace/_agent_code.py", code)
+        res = sandbox.commands.run(
+            "python3 /workspace/_agent_code.py", user="root", timeout=120
+        )
+        out: list[str] = []
+        if res.stdout:
+            out.append(res.stdout)
+        if res.stderr:
+            out.append("stderr:\n" + res.stderr)
+        if not out:
+            out.append(f"(exit code {res.exit_code})" if res.exit_code != 0 else "(no output)")
+        return "\n".join(out)
+    finally:
+        if sandbox is not None:
+            try:
+                sandbox.kill()
+            except Exception:
+                pass  # cleanup failure must not mask the original exception
+```
+
+### 5. Run the agent
+
+```python
+from langchain_openai import ChatOpenAI
+from langchain_core.messages import HumanMessage
+from langgraph.prebuilt import create_react_agent
+
+llm = ChatOpenAI(
+    model=os.getenv("CHAT_MODEL", "deepseek-v3"),
+    api_key=os.getenv("OPENAI_API_KEY") or os.getenv("TOKENHUB_API_KEY"),
+    base_url=os.getenv("OPENAI_BASE_URL", "https://tokenhub.tencentmaas.com/v1"),
+    temperature=0,
+)

+
+# LangChain 集成指南
+
+[English](../../guide/integrations/langchain.md)
+
+将调用 Python 工具的 [LangChain](https://github.com/langchain-ai/langchain) Agent 运行在
+[CubeSandbox](https://github.com/TencentCloud/CubeSandbox) 的 MicroVM 中。由于 Cube 暴露了
+**与 E2B 兼容的 API**，把 LangChain 应用从 E2B 迁移到 Cube 通常只需改一个环境变量，同时还能为
+Agent 生成的每一行代码获得 KVM 级隔离。本文附带可运行的
+[`examples/langchain-integration`](https://github.com/TencentCloud/CubeSandbox/tree/master/examples/langchain-integration)
+示例工程。
+
+## 集成对象与版本
+
+| 组件 | 版本 |
+|---|---|
+| LangChain | `langchain` `>= 0.3` |
+| langchain-openai | `>= 0.2` |
+| LangGraph（预置 ReAct Agent） | `langgraph` `>= 0.2` |
+| E2B SDK（E2B 兼容驱动） | `e2b`（最新） |
+| CubeSandbox 基础镜像 | `ghcr.io/tencentcloud/cubesandbox-base:2026.16` |
+| CubeSandbox 平台 | `>= 0.3.0` |
+
+## 前置条件
+
+- 已部署 CubeSandbox，CubeAPI 可从 `http://<node>:3000` 访问。
+- `$PATH` 中包含 `cubemastercli`，并已连接到集群。
+- 构建工作站已安装 Docker，且 Cube 节点可拉取的镜像仓库。
+- 一个 OpenAI 兼容的 LLM 端点（示例使用 TokenHub；任何 OpenAI 兼容端点均可经
+  `OPENAI_BASE_URL` / `OPENAI_API_KEY` 接入）。
+- 主机驱动脚本需要 Python 3.10+。
+
+## 为什么把 LangChain Agent 放进沙箱
+
+LangChain Agent 经常会暴露代码执行工具（数据分析、文件转换、调用 shell）。在宿主机上运行该工具，
+会把 Agent 的影响范围与你的开发机混在一起。放进 CubeSandbox 后，你将获得：
+
+| 关注点 | CubeSandbox 提供 |
+|---|---|
+| **隔离** | 每个会话一个 KVM MicroVM，独立客户机内核——Agent 代码无法触碰宿主机 |
+| **可复现** | 每次会话都从同一个模板快照启动 |
+| **快速启动** | 冷启动低于 60ms，因此并行跑多个 Agent 成本很低 |
+| **长任务** | `sandbox.pause()` 快照 VM + 根文件系统，稍后恢复 |
+| **密钥卫生** | CubeEgress 可在网络层注入 LLM 鉴权头——VM 内永远看不到真实密钥 |
+| **出口审计** | 每一次出站请求都会记录到出口审计日志 |
+
+## 接入步骤
+
+### 1. 构建模板镜像
+
+在 `cubesandbox-base` 之上叠加 Python 数据科学栈（envd 已在 `:49983` 监听）。
+
+```dockerfile
+# examples/langchain-integration/Dockerfile
+ARG CUBE_BASE_IMAGE=ghcr.io/tencentcloud/cubesandbox-base:2026.16
+FROM ${CUBE_BASE_IMAGE}
+
+ARG DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive
+
+RUN apt-get update \
+    && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
+        python3 python3-pip python3-venv ca-certificates git \
+    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*
+
+# 为可复现构建锁定版本，按需升级
+RUN python3 -m pip install --no-cache-dir --break-system-packages \
+        pandas==2.2.3 numpy==1.26.4 matplotlib==3.9.3 scikit-learn==1.6.1
+
+WORKDIR /workspace
+
+# 预置演示数据集，使示例 Agent 无需外部输入即可运行
+COPY sales.csv /workspace/sales.csv
+
+EXPOSE 49983
+```
+
+构建并推送：
+
+```bash
+docker build --platform linux/amd64 \
+  -t <your-registry>/langchain-cube:latest \
+  examples/langchain-integration
+docker push <your-registry>/langchain-cube:latest
+```
+
+### 2. 注册为 Cube 模板
+
+```bash
+cubemastercli tpl create-from-image \
+  --image <your-registry>/langchain-cube:latest \
+  --writable-layer-size 2G \
+  --expose-port 49983 \
+  --probe       49983 \
+  --probe-path  /health
+
+cubemastercli tpl watch --job-id <job_id>
+```
+
+任务进入 `READY` 后，记下 `template_id`——每次 `Sandbox.create()` 都要传入它。`2G` 可写层适合中等
+分析任务；若 Agent 运行时安装大体积包，可调到 `4G+`。
+
+### 3. 安装依赖并配置环境变量
+
+```bash
+cd examples/langchain-integration
+cp .env.example .env
+# 填写 E2B_API_URL（CubeAPI）、E2B_API_KEY、CUBE_TEMPLATE_ID 以及你的 LLM 密钥
+pip install -r requirements.txt
+```
+
+| 变量 | 流向 | 说明 |
+|---|---|---|
+| `E2B_API_URL` | 本地进程 | CubeAPI 地址（`http://<node>:3000`） |
+| `E2B_API_KEY` | 本地进程 | 本地开发填任意非空字符串 |
+| `CUBE_TEMPLATE_ID` | `Sandbox.create(template=...)` | 来自步骤 2 |
+| `OPENAI_API_KEY` / `TOKENHUB_API_KEY` | LLM 客户端 | OpenAI 兼容密钥 |
+| `OPENAI_BASE_URL` | LLM 客户端 | 如 `https://tokenhub.tencentmaas.com/v1` |
+| `CHAT_MODEL` | LLM 客户端 | 如 `deepseek-v3` |
+| `CUBE_SSL_CERT_FILE` | 本地进程 | （可选）HTTPS CubeAPI 的 CA 证书路径 |
+
+### 4. 把代码执行工具接到 Cube
+
+Agent 本身不变，只是工具体从本地 REPL 换成 Cube 沙箱。
+
+```python
+# langchain_agent_demo.py（节选——环境变量校验与工具定义）
+import os
+from dotenv import load_dotenv
+
+load_dotenv()
+# load_dotenv 后，脚本会校验 CUBE_TEMPLATE_ID、E2B_API_KEY、LLM API key，
+# 然后：
+import e2b.envd.rpc as _e2b_rpc
+_e2b_rpc.default_username = "root"   # Cube 的 envd 只服务 root
+
+from e2b import Sandbox                       # E2B 兼容；连接 CubeAPI
+from langchain_core.tools import tool
+
+
+@tool
+def run_python(code: str) -> str:
+    """在 Cube Sandbox MicroVM 内执行 Python，并返回 stdout/stderr。"""
+    sandbox = None
+    try:
+        sandbox = Sandbox.create(
+            template=os.environ["CUBE_TEMPLATE_ID"], timeout=300
+        )
+        sandbox.files.write("/workspace/_agent_code.py", code)
+        res = sandbox.commands.run(
+            "python3 /workspace/_agent_code.py", user="root", timeout=120
+        )
+        out: list[str] = []
+        if res.stdout:
+            out.append(res.stdout)
+        if res.stderr:
+            out.append("stderr:\n" + res.stderr)
+        if not out:
+            out.append(f"(exit code {res.exit_code})" if res.exit_code != 0 else "(无输出)")
+        return "\n".join(out)
+    finally:
+        if sandbox is not None:
+            try:
+                sandbox.kill()
+            except Exception:
+                pass  # 清理失败不能掩盖原始异常
+```
+
+### 5. 运行 Agent
+
+```python
+from langchain_openai import ChatOpenAI
+from langchain_core.messages import HumanMessage
+from langgraph.prebuilt import create_react_agent
+
+llm = ChatOpenAI(
+    model=os.getenv("CHAT_MODEL", "deepseek-v3"),
+    api_key=os.getenv("OPENAI_API_KEY") or os.getenv("TOKENHUB_API_KEY"),
+    base_url=os.getenv("OPENAI_BASE_URL", "https://tokenhub.tencentmaas.com/v1"),
+    temperature=0,
+)
