+# LangChain Integration Guide
+
+[中文文档](../../zh/guide/integrations/langchain.md)
+
+Run a [LangChain](https://github.com/langchain-ai/langchain) agent — whose tools execute
+Python — inside [CubeSandbox](https://github.com/TencentCloud/CubeSandbox) MicroVMs. Because
+Cube exposes an **E2B-compatible API**, moving a LangChain app from E2B to Cube is usually a
+single environment-variable change, while gaining KVM-level isolation for every line of
+agent-generated code. This guide ships with a runnable
+[`examples/langchain-integration`](https://github.com/TencentCloud/CubeSandbox/tree/master/examples/langchain-integration)
+project.
+
+## Integration Target and Version
+
+| Component | Version |
+|---|---|
+| LangChain | `langchain` `>= 0.3` |
+| langchain-openai | `>= 0.2` |
+| LangGraph (prebuilt ReAct agent) | `langgraph` `>= 0.2` |
+| E2B SDK (E2B-compatible driver) | `e2b` (latest) |
+| CubeSandbox base image | `ghcr.io/tencentcloud/cubesandbox-base:2026.16` |
+| CubeSandbox platform | `>= 0.3.0` |
+
+## Prerequisites
+
+- A running CubeSandbox deployment; CubeAPI reachable at `http://<node>:3000`.
+- `cubemastercli` on `$PATH`, connected to the cluster.
+- Docker on the build workstation, plus a registry the Cube nodes can pull from.
+- An OpenAI-compatible LLM endpoint (TokenHub is used in the example; any
+  OpenAI-compatible endpoint works via `OPENAI_BASE_URL` / `OPENAI_API_KEY`).
+- Python 3.10+ for the host driver scripts.
+
+## Why Run LangChain Agents Inside a Sandbox
+
+LangChain agents frequently expose a code-execution tool (data analysis, file transforms,
+shelling out). Running that tool on the host blends the agent's blast radius with your dev
+machine. Running it inside CubeSandbox gives you:
+
+| Concern | CubeSandbox provides |
+|---|---|
+| **Isolation** | KVM MicroVM per session, dedicated guest kernel — agent code cannot touch the host |
+| **Reproducibility** | Every session boots from the same template snapshot |
+| **Fast spin-up** | Sub-60 ms cold start, so many parallel agents are cheap |
+| **Long tasks** | `sandbox.pause()` snapshots VM + rootfs; resume later |
+| **Key hygiene** | CubeEgress can inject the LLM auth header on the wire — the VM never sees the real key |
+| **Egress audit** | Every outbound request is recorded in the egress audit log |
+
+## Integration Steps
+
+### 1. Build the template image
+
+The image stacks a Python data-science stack on top of `cubesandbox-base` (envd already
+listens on `:49983`).
+
+```dockerfile
+# examples/langchain-integration/Dockerfile
+ARG CUBE_BASE_IMAGE=ghcr.io/tencentcloud/cubesandbox-base:2026.16
+FROM ${CUBE_BASE_IMAGE}
+
+ARG DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive
+
+RUN apt-get update \
+    && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
+        python3 python3-pip python3-venv ca-certificates git \
+    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*
+
+# Pin data-science versions for reproducible builds. Bump as needed.
+RUN python3 -m pip install --no-cache-dir --break-system-packages \
+        pandas==2.2.3 numpy==1.26.4 matplotlib==3.9.3 scikit-learn==1.6.1
+
+WORKDIR /workspace
+
+# Pre-seed a demo dataset so the example agent can run without external inputs.
+COPY sales.csv /workspace/sales.csv
+
+EXPOSE 49983
+```
+
+Build and push:
+
+```bash
+docker build --platform linux/amd64 \
+  -t <your-registry>/langchain-cube:latest \
+  examples/langchain-integration
+docker push <your-registry>/langchain-cube:latest
+```
+
+### 2. Register as a Cube template
+
+```bash
+cubemastercli tpl create-from-image \
+  --image <your-registry>/langchain-cube:latest \
+  --writable-layer-size 2G \
+  --expose-port 49983 \
+  --probe       49983 \
+  --probe-path  /health
+
+cubemastercli tpl watch --job-id <job_id>
+```
+
+Once the job reaches `READY`, note the `template_id` — you pass it to every
+`Sandbox.create()` call. `2G` writable layer suits medium analysis tasks; bump to `4G+`
+if the agent installs large packages at runtime.
+
+### 3. Install dependencies and configure env
+
+```bash
+cd examples/langchain-integration
+cp .env.example .env
+# fill in E2B_API_URL (CubeAPI), E2B_API_KEY, CUBE_TEMPLATE_ID, and your LLM key
+pip install -r requirements.txt
+```
+
+| Variable | Where it flows | Notes |
+|---|---|---|
+| `E2B_API_URL` | Local process | CubeAPI address (`http://<node>:3000`) |
+| `E2B_API_KEY` | Local process | Any non-empty string in local dev |
+| `CUBE_TEMPLATE_ID` | `Sandbox.create(template=...)` | From step 2 |
+| `OPENAI_API_KEY` / `TOKENHUB_API_KEY` | LLM client | OpenAI-compatible key |
+| `OPENAI_BASE_URL` | LLM client | e.g. `https://tokenhub.tencentmaas.com/v1` |
+| `CHAT_MODEL` | LLM client | e.g. `deepseek-v3` |
+| `CUBE_SSL_CERT_FILE` | Local process | Optional CA bundle for HTTPS CubeAPI |
+
+### 4. Wire the code-execution tool to Cube
+
+The agent is unchanged; only the tool body swaps from a local REPL to a Cube Sandbox.
+
+```python
+# langchain_agent_demo.py (excerpt — env validation and tool definition)
+import os
+from dotenv import load_dotenv
+
+load_dotenv()
+# After load_dotenv, the script validates CUBE_TEMPLATE_ID, E2B_API_KEY,
+# and the LLM API key, then:
+import e2b.envd.rpc as _e2b_rpc
+_e2b_rpc.default_username = "root"   # Cube's envd serves only root
+
+from e2b import Sandbox                       # E2B-compatible; talks to CubeAPI
+from langchain_core.tools import tool
+
+
+@tool
+def run_python(code: str) -> str:
+    """Execute Python inside a Cube Sandbox MicroVM and return stdout/stderr."""
+    sandbox = None
+    try:
+        sandbox = Sandbox.create(
+            template=os.environ["CUBE_TEMPLATE_ID"], timeout=300
+        )
+        sandbox.files.write("/workspace/_agent_code.py", code)
+        res = sandbox.commands.run(
+            "python3 /workspace/_agent_code.py", user="root", timeout=120
+        )
+        out: list[str] = []
+        if res.stdout:
+            out.append(res.stdout)
+        if res.stderr:
+            out.append("stderr:\n" + res.stderr)
+        if not out:
+            out.append(f"(exit code {res.exit_code})" if res.exit_code != 0 else "(no output)")
+        return "\n".join(out)
+    finally:
+        if sandbox is not None:
+            try:
+                sandbox.kill()
+            except Exception:
+                pass  # cleanup failure must not mask the original exception
+```
+
+### 5. Run the agent
+
+```python
+from langchain_openai import ChatOpenAI
+from langchain_core.messages import HumanMessage
+from langgraph.prebuilt import create_react_agent
+
+llm = ChatOpenAI(
+    model=os.getenv("CHAT_MODEL", "deepseek-v3"),
+    api_key=os.getenv("OPENAI_API_KEY") or os.getenv("TOKENHUB_API_KEY"),
+    base_url=os.getenv("OPENAI_BASE_URL", "https://tokenhub.tencentmaas.com/v1"),
+    temperature=0,
+)

+"""LangChain agent running tool-generated Python code inside Cube Sandbox.
+
+Ports the E2B code-execution pattern to Cube Sandbox (E2B-compatible API). The
+agent exposes a single `run_python` tool; every snippet it emits runs inside a
+KVM MicroVM, so the host is never touched by agent-generated code.
+
+What it shows
+-------------
+- A Cube (E2B-compatible) `Sandbox` used as the execution backend for a
+  LangChain tool.
+- A ReAct agent built with LangGraph's `create_react_agent`.
+- The near-zero-refactor story: point `E2B_API_URL` at CubeAPI and the existing
+  E2B code path works unchanged.
+
+Usage
+-----
+    cp .env.example .env   # fill in real values
+    pip install -r requirements.txt
+    python langchain_agent_demo.py
+    python langchain_agent_demo.py --question "Train a linear model and report RMSE."
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import argparse
+import os
+import sys
+
+from dotenv import load_dotenv
+
+load_dotenv()
+
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# CUBE_SSL_CERT_FILE → SSL_CERT_FILE (for HTTPS CubeAPI deployments)
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+_cube_ssl = os.environ.get("CUBE_SSL_CERT_FILE")
+if _cube_ssl and os.path.isfile(_cube_ssl):
+    os.environ["SSL_CERT_FILE"] = _cube_ssl
+
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Environment variable validation — fail fast with clear messages
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+_REQUIRED_ENV = {
+    "CUBE_TEMPLATE_ID": "set CUBE_TEMPLATE_ID=<template-id> in .env",
+    "E2B_API_KEY": "set E2B_API_KEY=<any-non-empty-string> in .env",
+}
+_UNSET = []
+for var, hint in _REQUIRED_ENV.items():
+    if not os.environ.get(var):
+        _UNSET.append(f"  {var} — {hint}")
+if _UNSET:
+    print("Missing required environment variables:", file=sys.stderr)
+    print("\n".join(_UNSET), file=sys.stderr)
+    sys.exit(1)
+
+_api_key = os.getenv("OPENAI_API_KEY") or os.getenv("TOKENHUB_API_KEY")
+if not _api_key:
+    print(
+        "Missing LLM API key. Set either OPENAI_API_KEY or TOKENHUB_API_KEY in .env",
+        file=sys.stderr,
+    )
+    sys.exit(1)
+
+import e2b.envd.rpc as _e2b_rpc
+
+# Cube's envd serves only the "root" user. The E2B SDK defaults to "user",
+# so configure the RPC layer to target root for all filesystem operations.
+# This must happen before any Filesystem is constructed.
+_e2b_rpc.default_username = "root"
+
+from e2b import Sandbox  # E2B-compatible; talks to CubeAPI via E2B_API_URL
+from langchain_core.messages import HumanMessage
+from langchain_core.tools import tool
+from langchain_openai import ChatOpenAI
+from langgraph.prebuilt import create_react_agent
+
+
+@tool
+def run_python(code: str) -> str:
+    """Execute a Python snippet inside a Cube Sandbox MicroVM and return stdout/stderr.
+
+    Use this to compute with pandas/numpy/matplotlib, read files under
+    /workspace, or install nothing (the stack is preinstalled in the template).
+
+    The template image pre-seeds /workspace/sales.csv so the default demo
+    question works without external inputs.
+    """
+    sandbox = None
+    try:
+        sandbox = Sandbox.create(
+            template=os.environ["CUBE_TEMPLATE_ID"], timeout=300
+        )
+        sandbox.files.write("/workspace/_agent_code.py", code)
+        res = sandbox.commands.run(
+            "python3 /workspace/_agent_code.py", user="root", timeout=120
+        )
+        out: list[str] = []
+        if res.stdout:
+            out.append(res.stdout)
+        if res.stderr:
+            out.append("stderr:\n" + res.stderr)
+        if not out:
+            # Distinguish "no output" from "non-zero exit with nothing printed"
+            if res.exit_code != 0:
+                out.append(f"(exit code {res.exit_code})")
+            else:
+                out.append("(no output)")
+        return "\n".join(out)

**Suggestion:** Warn when overwriting an existing `SSL_CERT_FILE`.

Line 38 unconditionally sets `os.environ["SSL_CERT_FILE"]`, silently overwriting any pre-existing value the user may have set for other purposes (corporate proxy, internal PKI). After this line, all SSL connections in the process use the Cube sandbox CA bundle, which may not include the user's original trust roots.

Consider:
```python
if _cube_ssl and os.path.isfile(_cube_ssl):
    existing = os.environ.get("SSL_CERT_FILE")
    if existing is not None and existing != _cube_ssl:
        print("WARNING: CUBE_SSL_CERT_FILE overrides previously set SSL_CERT_FILE.", file=sys.stderr)
    os.environ["SSL_CERT_FILE"] = _cube_ssl
```

review_comments.body:
**Suggestion:** Log a warning instead of silently swallowing the exception.

If `sandbox.kill()` fails (network blip, node overload), the failure is completely invisible. During development this makes it hard to diagnose resource leaks. A stderr warning keeps the original exception unshadowed (the warning fires after the return/exception path is already decided) but gives operators visibility into cleanup failures.

```python
except Exception:
    import sys
    import traceback
    print("Warning: failed to kill sandbox:", traceback.format_exc(), file=sys.stderr)
```

+Ports the E2B code-execution pattern to Cube Sandbox (E2B-compatible API). The
+agent exposes a single `run_python` tool; every snippet it emits runs inside a
+KVM MicroVM, so the host is never touched by agent-generated code.
+
+What it shows
+-------------
+- A Cube (E2B-compatible) `Sandbox` used as the execution backend for a
+  LangChain tool.
+- A ReAct agent built with LangGraph's `create_react_agent`.
+- The near-zero-refactor story: point `E2B_API_URL` at CubeAPI and the existing
+  E2B code path works unchanged.
+
+Usage
+-----
+    cp .env.example .env   # fill in real values
+    pip install -r requirements.txt
+    python langchain_agent_demo.py
+    python langchain_agent_demo.py --question "Train a linear model and report RMSE."
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import argparse
+import os
+import sys
+
+from dotenv import load_dotenv
+
+load_dotenv()
+
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# CUBE_SSL_CERT_FILE → SSL_CERT_FILE (for HTTPS CubeAPI deployments)
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+_cube_ssl = os.environ.get("CUBE_SSL_CERT_FILE")
+if _cube_ssl and os.path.isfile(_cube_ssl):
+    os.environ["SSL_CERT_FILE"] = _cube_ssl
+
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Environment variable validation — fail fast with clear messages
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+_REQUIRED_ENV = {
+    "CUBE_TEMPLATE_ID": "set CUBE_TEMPLATE_ID=<template-id> in .env",
+    "E2B_API_KEY": "set E2B_API_KEY=<any-non-empty-string> in .env",
+}
+_UNSET = []
+for var, hint in _REQUIRED_ENV.items():
+    if not os.environ.get(var):
+        _UNSET.append(f"  {var} — {hint}")
+if _UNSET:
+    print("Missing required environment variables:", file=sys.stderr)
+    print("\n".join(_UNSET), file=sys.stderr)
+    sys.exit(1)
+
+_api_key = os.getenv("OPENAI_API_KEY") or os.getenv("TOKENHUB_API_KEY")
+if not _api_key:
+    print(
+        "Missing LLM API key. Set either OPENAI_API_KEY or TOKENHUB_API_KEY in .env",
+        file=sys.stderr,
+    )
+    sys.exit(1)
+
+import e2b.envd.rpc as _e2b_rpc
+
+# Cube's envd serves only the "root" user. The E2B SDK defaults to "user",
+# so configure the RPC layer to target root for all filesystem operations.
+# This must happen before any Filesystem is constructed.
+_e2b_rpc.default_username = "root"
+
+from e2b import Sandbox  # E2B-compatible; talks to CubeAPI via E2B_API_URL
+from langchain_core.messages import HumanMessage
+from langchain_core.tools import tool
+from langchain_openai import ChatOpenAI
+from langgraph.prebuilt import create_react_agent
+
+
+@tool
+def run_python(code: str) -> str:
+    """Execute a Python snippet inside a Cube Sandbox MicroVM and return stdout/stderr.
+
+    Use this to compute with pandas/numpy/matplotlib, read files under
+    /workspace, or install nothing (the stack is preinstalled in the template).
+
+    The template image pre-seeds /workspace/sales.csv so the default demo
+    question works without external inputs.
+    """
+    sandbox = None
+    try:
+        sandbox = Sandbox.create(
+            template=os.environ["CUBE_TEMPLATE_ID"], timeout=300
+        )
+        sandbox.files.write("/workspace/_agent_code.py", code)
+        res = sandbox.commands.run(
+            "python3 /workspace/_agent_code.py", user="root", timeout=120
+        )
+        out: list[str] = []
+        if res.stdout:
+            out.append(res.stdout)
+        if res.stderr:
+            out.append("stderr:\n" + res.stderr)
+        if not out:
+            # Distinguish "no output" from "non-zero exit with nothing printed"
+            if res.exit_code != 0:
+                out.append(f"(exit code {res.exit_code})")
+            else:
+                out.append("(no output)")
+        return "\n".join(out)
+    finally:
+        if sandbox is not None:
+            try:
+                sandbox.kill()
+            except Exception:
+                pass  # cleanup failure must not mask the original exception

E2B SDK lacks a per-connection CA override API. It only reads SSL_CERT_FILE from the environment; there is no per-session certificate option.

Fixing this would require changing the SDK or connection pattern — cost far outweighs benefit.

+# LangChain Integration Guide
+
+[中文文档](../../zh/guide/integrations/langchain.md)
+
+Run a [LangChain](https://github.com/langchain-ai/langchain) agent — whose tools execute
+Python — inside [CubeSandbox](https://github.com/TencentCloud/CubeSandbox) MicroVMs. Because
+Cube exposes an **E2B-compatible API**, moving a LangChain app from E2B to Cube is usually a
+single environment-variable change, while gaining KVM-level isolation for every line of
+agent-generated code. This guide ships with a runnable
+[`examples/langchain-integration`](https://github.com/TencentCloud/CubeSandbox/tree/master/examples/langchain-integration)
+project.
+
+## Integration Target and Version
+
+| Component | Version |
+|---|---|
+| LangChain | `langchain` `>= 0.3` |
+| langchain-openai | `>= 0.2` |
+| LangGraph (prebuilt ReAct agent) | `langgraph` `>= 0.2` |
+| E2B SDK (E2B-compatible driver) | `e2b` (latest) |
+| CubeSandbox base image | `ghcr.io/tencentcloud/cubesandbox-base:2026.16` |
+| CubeSandbox platform | `>= 0.3.0` |
+
+## Prerequisites
+
+- A running CubeSandbox deployment; CubeAPI reachable at `http://<node>:3000`.
+- `cubemastercli` on `$PATH`, connected to the cluster.
+- Docker on the build workstation, plus a registry the Cube nodes can pull from.
+- An OpenAI-compatible LLM endpoint (TokenHub is used in the example; any
+  OpenAI-compatible endpoint works via `OPENAI_BASE_URL` / `OPENAI_API_KEY`).
+- Python 3.10+ for the host driver scripts.
+
+## Why Run LangChain Agents Inside a Sandbox
+
+LangChain agents frequently expose a code-execution tool (data analysis, file transforms,
+shelling out). Running that tool on the host blends the agent's blast radius with your dev
+machine. Running it inside CubeSandbox gives you:
+
+| Concern | CubeSandbox provides |
+|---|---|
+| **Isolation** | KVM MicroVM per session, dedicated guest kernel — agent code cannot touch the host |
+| **Reproducibility** | Every session boots from the same template snapshot |
+| **Fast spin-up** | Sub-60 ms cold start, so many parallel agents are cheap |
+| **Long tasks** | `sandbox.pause()` snapshots VM + rootfs; resume later |
+| **Key hygiene** | CubeEgress can inject the LLM auth header on the wire — the VM never sees the real key |
+| **Egress audit** | Every outbound request is recorded in the egress audit log |
+
+## Integration Steps
+
+### 1. Build the template image
+
+The image stacks a Python data-science stack on top of `cubesandbox-base` (envd already
+listens on `:49983`).
+
+```dockerfile
+# examples/langchain-integration/Dockerfile
+ARG CUBE_BASE_IMAGE=ghcr.io/tencentcloud/cubesandbox-base:2026.16
+FROM ${CUBE_BASE_IMAGE}
+
+ARG DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive
+
+RUN apt-get update \
+    && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
+        python3 python3-pip python3-venv ca-certificates git \
+    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*
+
+RUN python3 -m pip install --no-cache-dir --break-system-packages \
+        pandas numpy matplotlib scikit-learn
+
+WORKDIR /workspace
+
+# Pre-seed a demo dataset so the example agent can run without external inputs.
+COPY sales.csv /workspace/sales.csv
+
+EXPOSE 49983
+```
+
+Build and push:
+
+```bash
+docker build --platform linux/amd64 \
+  -t <your-registry>/langchain-cube:latest \
+  examples/langchain-integration
+docker push <your-registry>/langchain-cube:latest
+```
+
+### 2. Register as a Cube template
+
+```bash
+cubemastercli tpl create-from-image \
+  --image <your-registry>/langchain-cube:latest \
+  --writable-layer-size 2G \
+  --expose-port 49983 \
+  --probe       49983 \
+  --probe-path  /health
+
+cubemastercli tpl watch --job-id <job_id>
+```
+
+Once the job reaches `READY`, note the `template_id` — you pass it to every
+`Sandbox.create()` call. `2G` writable layer suits medium analysis tasks; bump to `4G+`
+if the agent installs large packages at runtime.
+
+### 3. Install dependencies and configure env
+
+```bash
+cd examples/langchain-integration
+cp .env.example .env
+# fill in E2B_API_URL (CubeAPI), E2B_API_KEY, CUBE_TEMPLATE_ID, and your LLM key
+pip install -r requirements.txt
+```
+
+| Variable | Where it flows | Notes |
+|---|---|---|
+| `E2B_API_URL` | Local process | CubeAPI address (`http://<node>:3000`) |
+| `E2B_API_KEY` | Local process | Any non-empty string in local dev |
+| `CUBE_TEMPLATE_ID` | `Sandbox.create(template=...)` | From step 2 |
+| `OPENAI_API_KEY` / `TOKENHUB_API_KEY` | LLM client | OpenAI-compatible key |
+| `OPENAI_BASE_URL` | LLM client | e.g. `https://tokenhub.tencentmaas.com/v1` |
+| `CHAT_MODEL` | LLM client | e.g. `deepseek-v3` |
+| `CUBE_SSL_CERT_FILE` | Local process | Optional CA bundle for HTTPS CubeAPI |
+
+### 4. Wire the code-execution tool to Cube

+The agent is unchanged; only the tool body swaps from a local REPL to a Cube Sandbox.

+```python

+# and the LLM API key, then:

+_e2b_rpc.default_username = "root"   # Cube's envd serves only root
+
+from e2b import Sandbox                       # E2B-compatible; talks to CubeAPI
+from langchain_core.tools import tool
+
+
+@tool
+def run_python(code: str) -> str:
+    """Execute Python inside a Cube Sandbox MicroVM and return stdout/stderr."""
+    sandbox = None
+    try:
+        sandbox = Sandbox.create(
+            template=os.environ["CUBE_TEMPLATE_ID"], timeout=300
+        )
+        sandbox.files.write("/workspace/_agent_code.py", code)
+        res = sandbox.commands.run(
+            "python3 /workspace/_agent_code.py", user="root", timeout=120
+        )
+        out: list[str] = []
+        if res.stdout:
+            out.append(res.stdout)
+        if res.stderr:
+            out.append("stderr:\n" + res.stderr)
+        if not out:
+            out.append(f"(exit code {res.exit_code})" if res.exit_code != 0 else "(no output)")
+        return "\n".join(out)
+    finally:
+        if sandbox is not None:
+            try:
+                sandbox.kill()
+            except Exception:
+                pass  # cleanup failure must not mask the original exception
+```
+
+### 5. Run the agent
+
+```python
+from langchain_openai import ChatOpenAI
+from langchain_core.messages import HumanMessage
+from langgraph.prebuilt import create_react_agent
+
+llm = ChatOpenAI(
+    model=os.getenv("CHAT_MODEL", "deepseek-v3"),
+    api_key=os.getenv("OPENAI_API_KEY") or os.getenv("TOKENHUB_API_KEY"),

**Global `SSL_CERT_FILE` override is broader than necessary**

Setting `os.environ["SSL_CERT_FILE"]` affects ALL HTTPS connections from this process — not just those to CubeAPI. If the custom CA bundle doesn't include standard root CAs (common for self-hosted deployments), LLM endpoint TLS will also fail with a confusing error. Consider scoping the CA override to only the CubeAPI connection (e.g., via a per-client SSL context), or adding a comment warning users about the process-wide scope.

+## 为什么把 LangChain Agent 放进沙箱

+LangChain Agent 经常会暴露代码执行工具（数据分析、文件转换、调用 shell）。在宿主机上运行该工具，

+|---|---|
+| **隔离** | 每个会话一个 KVM MicroVM，独立客户机内核——Agent 代码无法触碰宿主机 |
+| **可复现** | 每次会话都从同一个模板快照启动 |
+| **快速启动** | 冷启动低于 60ms，因此并行跑多个 Agent 成本很低 |
+| **长任务** | `sandbox.pause()` 快照 VM + 根文件系统，稍后恢复 |
+| **密钥卫生** | CubeEgress 可在网络层注入 LLM 鉴权头——VM 内永远看不到真实密钥 |
+| **出口审计** | 每一次出站请求都会记录到出口审计日志 |

+### 1. 构建模板镜像

+FROM ${CUBE_BASE_IMAGE}
+
+ARG DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive
+
+RUN apt-get update \
+    && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
+        python3 python3-pip python3-venv ca-certificates git \
+    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*
+
+RUN python3 -m pip install --no-cache-dir --break-system-packages \
+        pandas numpy matplotlib scikit-learn
+
+WORKDIR /workspace
+
+# 预置演示数据集，使示例 Agent 无需外部输入即可运行
+COPY sales.csv /workspace/sales.csv
+
+EXPOSE 49983
+```
+
+构建并推送：
+
+```bash
+docker build --platform linux/amd64 \
+  -t <your-registry>/langchain-cube:latest \
+  examples/langchain-integration
+docker push <your-registry>/langchain-cube:latest
+```
+
+### 2. 注册为 Cube 模板
+
+```bash
+cubemastercli tpl create-from-image \
+  --image <your-registry>/langchain-cube:latest \
+  --writable-layer-size 2G \
+  --expose-port 49983 \
+  --probe       49983 \
+  --probe-path  /health
+
+cubemastercli tpl watch --job-id <job_id>
+```
+
+任务进入 `READY` 后，记下 `template_id`——每次 `Sandbox.create()` 都要传入它。`2G` 可写层适合中等
+分析任务；若 Agent 运行时安装大体积包，可调到 `4G+`。

+# 填写 E2B_API_URL（CubeAPI）、E2B_API_KEY、CUBE_TEMPLATE_ID 以及你的 LLM 密钥

+        )

**ChatOpenAI has no timeout — can hang indefinitely, leaking sandbox resources**

The `ChatOpenAI` constructor is called without a `timeout` or `max_retries` parameter. Under the hood (httpx), this means an indefinite wait if the LLM API hangs due to a network partition, rate-limiting stall, or server-side issue. **New sandbox per ReAct turn loses state and adds latency**

`run_python` creates + kills a new `Sandbox` on every invocation. In a ReAct loop (typically 5–15 iterations per query), this means:
- State is lost between turns — the agent re-loads data and re-imports libraries on every call.
- Cumulative overhead from N sequential create/destroy cycles.

Other examples in this repo (e.g. `run_pi_agent.py`) create one sandbox and reuse it across the agent session. Consider either:
- Creating the sandbox once in `main()` and closing over it, or
- Adding a "Reuse a sandbox across agent turns" subsection to the guide's "Going Further" section with a closure or context-manager pattern.

review_comments.body:
**Per-call sandbox create/destroy creates O(N) overhead for multi-step agents.**

Each invocation of this `@tool` creates, boots, and destroys a fresh MicroVM. A ReAct agent often makes 3–8+ tool calls per question, so it pays the full lifecycle cost every time.

A single sandbox reused across all tool calls is cheaper and equally isolated:
- Create the sandbox once before the agent loop
- Pass it into the tool via a closure or factory function
- Kill it after the agent finishes

Consider refactoring to something like:

```python
def make_run_python(sbx):
    @tool
    def run_python(code: str) -> str:
        sbx.files.write("/workspace/_agent_code.py", code)
        ...
    return run_python
```

This is also worth mentioning in the Caveats section of the guide — the per-tool-call pattern maximizes isolation at the cost of latency and cluster load.

review_comments.body:
**Unbound variable in `finally` block.** 

If `Sandbox.create()` raises an exception (e.g., network error, invalid template ID, auth failure), the variable `sandbox` is never assigned. The `finally` block still executes and `sandbox.kill()` raises `UnboundLocalError`, which **masks the original exception** — the caller sees a confusing name error instead of the root cause.

Fix: guard the finally block, or use a sentinel pattern:

```python
sandbox = None
try:
    sandbox = Sandbox.create(...)
    ...
finally:
    if sandbox is not None:
        sandbox.kill()
```

This is documented in the SDK's own test suite (`sdk/python/tests/test_sandbox.py`, lines 95-98) which expects `ApiError` to propagate cleanly.

**PEP 668 `externally-managed-environment` risk, no version pinning.**

On newer Debian/Ubuntu releases (Debian 12+, Ubuntu 23.04+) that enforce PEP 668, this `pip install` will fail because `python3-venv` is installed but never activated. The build breaks with an `externally-managed-environment` error unless `--break-system-packages` is passed or `PIP_REQUIRE_VIRTUALENV=false` is set.

Additionally, neither apt packages nor pip packages have version pins, making template builds non-reproducible over time — which contradicts the "Reproducibility" value proposition claimed in the guide.

Consider adding a venv activation step or pinning versions to match the guide's version table.

<!-- cubesandbox-auto-review:start -->
## Review: PR #951 — ch-remote: default snapshot type to full instead of incremental

### Overall assessment ✅

This is a clean, correct fix. The change aligns the CLI `--snapshot-type` default with the `SnapshotType` enum's `#[default] Full` in `vm-migration/src/lib.rs` and fixes a real bug where cold-start snapshots would fail with:

> `Base snapshot file not found at ..., incremental (pagemap_anon) snapshot requires an existing base file`

The diff is minimal (2 lines in 1 file) and well-scoped. No regressions are expected: downstream consumers (Cubelet, CubeShim) always pass `--snapshot-type` explicitly. Users who want the incremental or soft-dirty paths can opt in via `--snapshot-type incremental` / `--snapshot-type soft-dirty`.

### Drive-by: silent fallback on invalid `--snapshot-type` values

The parsing logic at `ch-remote.rs:289` uses `unwrap_or_default()`:

```rust
.map(|s| s.parse::<SnapshotType>().unwrap_or_default())
```

If a user passes `--snapshot-type garbage`, `parse()` returns `Err(...)` and `unwrap_or_default()` silently converts it to `SnapshotType::Full` with no warning. The user would believe they configured a specific mode but get `Full` instead.

Consider surfacing parse errors, e.g.:

```rust
.map(|s| s.parse::<SnapshotType>().unwrap_or_else(|e| {
    eprintln!("Warning: {e}, falling back to default snapshot type");
    SnapshotType::default()
}))
```

The rest of the function handles the other args via `unwrap()` on line 293, so the silent fallback stands out as an inconsistency. This is a pre-existing issue, not introduced by this PR, but the code paths are the same ones being modified.

### Summary

| Dimension | Verdict |
|-----------|---------|
| Code quality | Correct fix; minor pre-existing duplication between `snapshot` and `pause2snapshot` argument definitions |
| Security | No issues; safer default (full is self-contained vs incremental requires a base file) |
| Performance | Acceptable trade-off; users who want incremental opt in explicitly |
| Test coverage | Fix makes existing tests pass (`snapshot_and_check_events` never passed `--snapshot-type`); the flag itself has no dedicated integration test |

item.body:
The `snapshot` and `pause2snapshot` subcommands of ch-remote hardcoded `--snapshot-type` to `.default_value("incremental")`. This contradicted the `#[default]` marker on `SnapshotType::Full` in vm-migration and, more importantly, made every cold-start snapshot fail because the incremental (pagemap_anon) path requires a pre-existing base file at the destination:

    Cannot send VM snapshot: Failed to send migratable component
    snapshot: Base snapshot file not found at
    "/tmp/.../snapshot/memory-ranges", incremental (pagemap_anon)
    snapshot requires an existing base file

Integration tests that take a first snapshot via
`snapshot_and_check_events` (e.g.
`test_restored_vsock_accepts_new_passthrough_fd`) never pass `--snapshot-type`, so they consistently tripped this failure.

Change the CLI default back to `full` so that the unspecified case matches `SnapshotType::default()` and produces a self-contained memory image on the first snapshot. Users who want the incremental or soft-dirty paths can still opt in explicitly via `--snapshot-type incremental` / `--snapshot-type soft-dirty`. Also clarify the help text to note that `incremental` needs an existing base snapshot.

This PR correctly fixes a content-encoding passthrough bug in the E2B dev sidecar by configuring aiohttp's `ClientSession` with `auto_decompress=False` and `skip_auto_headers={hdrs.ACCEPT_ENCODING}`. The implementation is clean, minimal, and well-motivated — the inline comments clearly explain the "why" behind both configuration changes.

**1. Test coverage could be broadened for other content-encodings** (medium)
The production change disables auto-decompression globally via `auto_decompress=False`, which applies to all content-coding schemes (gzip, deflate, brotli, zstd, etc.). However, only gzip is tested. If the upstream ever returns `deflate` or `br`, the same raw-bytes-preservation behavior needs to hold. Consider parameterizing the `_content_encoding_proxy` fixture to cycle through a few common encodings. `test_http_proxy_does_not_inject_accept_encoding` does not assert `response.status == 200` while the other two new tests do. An inline comment has been posted with a suggestion.

- **Performance**: Positive change — decompression burden shifts from the proxy to the downstream client, reducing both CPU and bandwidth at the proxy layer. No regressions.

item.body:
## Summary

- preserve content-encoded response bytes and their representation metadata through the E2B dev sidecar
- avoid adding `Accept-Encoding` when the downstream client did not request content coding
- add regression coverage for gzip forwarding, normal client decoding, and encoding negotiation

## Reproduction

1. Configure `examples/e2b-dev-sidecar/.env` as described in its README, using a reachable CubeAPI, CubeProxy, and a valid template.
2. From `examples/e2b-dev-sidecar`, run:

```python
import os

from dotenv import load_dotenv

load_dotenv()

from dev_sidecar import setup_dev_sidecar

setup_dev_sidecar()

from e2b_code_interpreter import Sandbox

with Sandbox.create(template=os.environ["CUBE_TEMPLATE_ID"]) as sandbox:
    path = "/tmp/cube-sidecar-gzip.txt"
    sandbox.files.write(path, "sidecar gzip check")
    print(sandbox.files.read(path))
```

Expected: the file content is returned.

## Before fix

On the unmodified implementation:

- sandbox creation succeeded
- `sandbox.run_code(...)` succeeded
- `sandbox.files.read(...)` failed with `httpx.DecodingError` containing `incorrect header check`

The regression test added by this PR also fails before the fix: the sidecar sends an already-decoded response body while retaining `Content-Encoding: gzip`.

## Root cause

The proxy forwards the upstream `Content-Encoding` header, but its shared aiohttp `ClientSession` automatically decompresses response bodies by default. The downstream E2B/httpx client therefore receives decoded bytes labeled as gzip and attempts to decompress them a second time.

The same aiohttp session also adds `Accept-Encoding` by default when the downstream request omitted it, changing encoding negotiation at the proxy boundary.

## Fix

Configure the proxy-only aiohttp session to:

- use `auto_decompress=False`, keeping the response bytes consistent with `Content-Encoding` and representation metadata such as `ETag`
- skip automatic `Accept-Encoding` generation while continuing to forward an explicitly supplied downstream header

## After fix

The same deployed-cluster reproduction completed successfully:

- sandbox creation: passed
- `sandbox.run_code(...)`: passed
- `sandbox.commands.run(...)`: passed
- `sandbox.files.write(...)` and `sandbox.files.read(...)`: passed
- sandbox cleanup on context exit: passed

The reproduction prints `sidecar gzip check` as expected.

## Validation

Automated regression coverage verifies that:

- raw gzip bytes, `Content-Encoding`, `ETag`, and `Vary` are preserved through the proxy
- a normal httpx client decodes the response exactly once
- a request without `Accept-Encoding` is forwarded without the sidecar adding one

Commands run:

```text
cd examples/e2b-dev-sidecar
python3 -m pytest test_dev_sidecar.py -q
# 10 passed

python3 -m py_compile dev_sidecar.py test_dev_sidecar.py
git diff --check
```

A live E2B flow was also validated against a deployed CubeSandbox cluster using sandbox creation, code execution, command execution, file write/read, and cleanup.

## Scope

This change only affects the HTTP response path and content-coding negotiation in `examples/e2b-dev-sidecar`. CubeAPI and CubeProxy behavior are unchanged.

item.body:
## Summary

- bind every QEMU user-network host forward in `dev-env/run_vm.sh` explicitly to loopback
- make the VM's actual listeners match the localhost-only behavior documented by the dev-environment guides and printed at startup

## Reproduction

1. Start the development VM from an unmodified checkout:

```bash
cd dev-env
./run_vm.sh
```

2. In another terminal, inspect the listeners for the default forwarded ports:

```bash
ss -ltnp | grep -E ':(10022|13000|11080|11443|12088)\b'
```

The README and startup output identify these endpoints as `127.0.0.1`, but the unmodified QEMU arguments use `hostfwd=tcp::...`. QEMU interprets the omitted host address as a wildcard bind, so the listeners appear on `0.0.0.0` instead of loopback.

## Root cause

All five forwarding rules omit QEMU's optional `hostaddr` field:

```text
hostfwd=tcp::<host-port>-:<guest-port>
```

An empty `hostaddr` does not mean localhost. It allows QEMU to listen on every IPv4 interface, contrary to the existing documentation and log output.

## Fix

Set `hostaddr` to `127.0.0.1` in the SSH, Cube API, CubeProxy HTTP, CubeProxy HTTPS, and WebUI forwarding rules:

```text
hostfwd=tcp:127.0.0.1:<host-port>-:<guest-port>
```

## Before and after validation

Before the fix:

- the generated QEMU network argument contained five `hostfwd=tcp::...` rules
- a minimal QEMU user-network reproduction with an empty `hostaddr` listened on `0.0.0.0`

After the fix:

- the generated QEMU network argument contains five `hostfwd=tcp:127.0.0.1:...` rules
- the equivalent QEMU reproduction with an explicit host address listens only on `127.0.0.1`
- the documented localhost endpoints and startup output are unchanged and now match runtime behavior

## Validation

```text
bash -n dev-env/run_vm.sh
git diff --check
```

A stubbed QEMU invocation was also used to capture the argument generated by `run_vm.sh`; it confirmed that all five forwarding rules use explicit loopback addresses after the change. A separate minimal QEMU invocation confirmed the listener behavior for omitted and explicit host addresses, and all test processes were stopped afterward.

## Scope

This changes only the local QEMU development helper. It does not alter production deployment networking or make the forwarding address configurable.

## Review Summary for PR #948

### Overall Verdict: ✅ Approach is correct — ship with one follow-up

This PR correctly fixes a real bug: `ext_lib.new("subjectAltName", sans)` was silently producing SAN-less leaf certs because the API expects a config-syntax string, not an altname object. The fix uses `cert:set_subject_alt_name(sans)` (the purpose-built API) and adds proper error propagation.

All five specialized reviewers agreed:
- **Code quality:** Fix is clean, consistent with existing error-handling patterns, no unused imports
- **Security:** SAN branching (DNS vs IP vs fallback) handled correctly across all code paths
- **Performance:** Zero hot-path impact — SAN construction only runs on cache miss, already dominated by ECDSA key generation and signing
- **Documentation:** All code comments accurate; no external docs need updating
- **Test coverage:** No tests exist for `cert_signer.lua` — this bug is precisely the kind a unit test would have caught

### 🔔 Notable Finding (inline comment posted)

**Unchecked `add_extension` calls on lines 136–139** — the three remaining `cert:add_extension(ext_lib.new(...))` calls (basicConstraints, keyUsage, extendedKeyUsage) discard their return values. This is the same pattern that caused the SAN bug. A missing `basicConstraints=CA:FALSE` is the most concerning failure mode. Consider adding error checks to match the new SAN pattern.

### Minor observations (not blocking)

- **Empty SAN edge case:** If `sign_leaf` is called without both SNI and dst_ip, an empty altname object is passed to `set_subject_alt_name`. Unlikely in practice, but a guard would make the function more robust.
- **Serial number:** `math.random()` is never explicitly seeded in this module, and `bn_lib.new()` returning nil is silently ignored, yielding a zero serial (RFC 5280 non-conformant). Pre-existing.
- **Cache key collision:** An attacker-controlled SNI like `ip:10.0.0.1` could collide with the fallback key prefix. Pre-existing; low practical impact.

### Recommendation

Ship the fix as-is. The unchecked extensions finding is worth a follow-up but not a blocker — the SAN fix is clearly correct, well-documented, and addresses a real production issue.

item.body:
sign_leaf() built an altname object and passed it to ext_lib.new("subjectAltName", sans), but resty.openssl's x509.extension.new expects the value as a config-syntax *string* (e.g. "DNS:foo,IP:1.2.3.4") — it invokes X509V3_EXT_nconf_nid under the hood. Handed an altname object, it returns nil,err, and because the return value was never checked, cert:add_extension(nil) also silently failed. Result: leaf certs shipped with CN only and no SAN, so modern clients (which have ignored CN since RFC 2818 was deprecated by RFC 6125, and which Chrome/Firefox enforce strictly) rejected them with ERR_CERT_COMMON_NAME_INVALID.

Switch to x509:set_subject_alt_name(altname_obj), which is the purpose-built API that takes an altname instance directly, and check its return value so a future breakage surfaces loudly instead of producing SAN-less certs again.

    *  expire date: Jul 20 12:10:56 2026 GMT

After the fix:

    *  subjectAltName: host "www.deepseek.com" matched cert's "www.deepseek.com"

## Review: PR #946 — fix(cubelet): make nested host mount order deterministic

Overall this is a well-structured fix. The sorting logic is correct, the test coverage is thorough, and the E2E integration test validates the real-world nested-mount use case. A few optional observations below.

### Notable

**1. Unhandled `jsoniter.Marshal` errors persist in sibling functions** (virtiofs.go:89, 259)
The PR correctly fixes the previously-ignored marshal error in `generateRestoreVirtiofsOpt` (line 154–156). Two other functions in the same file still silently discard it: `generateSandboxVirtiofsOpt` at line 89 and `generateEmptyVirtiofsDevices` at line 259. Aligning these three to the same pattern would improve consistency.

**2. `sortRestoreVirtioMounts` mutates its argument as a side effect** (virtiofs.go:178–200)
The function both sorts `candidates` in-place via `sort.Slice` AND returns a new slice of a different type. While the sole caller passes a local variable, making the mutation harmless today, this dual behavior is surprising. Consider copying before sorting:

```go
sorted := append([]restoreVirtioMount(nil), candidates...)
sort.Slice(sorted, ...)
```

### Minor

**3. Missing capacity hints on map and slice** (virtiofs.go:112, 119)
`vmByVolName` and `restoreMounts` are built from known-length sources (`VolumeMounts` and `HostDirBackendInfos` respectively). Pre-allocating would avoid rehashing/growth overhead:

```go
vmByVolName := make(map[string]indexedVolumeMount, len(containerReq.GetVolumeMounts()))
restoreMounts := make([]restoreVirtioMount, 0, len(storageInfo.HostDirBackendInfos))
```

**4. `path.Clean` called O(n log n) times inside sort comparator** (virtiofs.go:180–181)
Each comparison re-computes `path.Clean` on both operands. Pre-computing cleaned destinations before sorting reduces this to O(n). Negligible at typical scale but a simple improvement.

**5. Untyped-nil vs typed-nil `StorageInfo` not tested** (virtiofs.go:103–106)
The `!ok || storageInfo == nil` guard correctly handles a typed-nil `*storage.StorageInfo` inside a non-nil interface, but there is no test for this scenario — a known Go gotcha that has caused production bugs.

Thanks for raising this. I agree that unrestricted nested mounts can be difficult to reason about and should probably be constrained.

We do have a concrete use case for them in Agent Teams, though. Each agent mounts the same team workspace read-only, then overlays its own subdirectory as writable:

```text
/workspace                    read-only team workspace
/workspace/agents/agent-a     writable for agent-a
```

This gives us a “shared readable, privately writable” model: all agents can read team inputs and artifacts, while each agent can modify only its own directory. This is especially useful because agents in the same team may run different environment templates.

Without nested mounts, we would need to expose the shared and private parts at unrelated paths or introduce a copy/synchronization layer, both of which complicate the application model.

Also, this PR does not introduce nested mounts—the current API already accepts them. It makes their restore-time behavior deterministic. Disallowing them would therefore be a separate validation and compatibility decision.

A constrained model could require canonical absolute destinations, deterministic parent-before-child mounting, explicit permission rules, and rejection of ambiguous destinations or overlapping writable mounts. Adding a restore-only rule would make validation inconsistent, and a raw substring check for .. would also reject legitimate path components such as ..cache. This PR does not broaden the accepted input or data flow, so I am keeping it scoped to deterministic restore ordering. Absolute-path and traversal-segment policy should be handled consistently in the centralized request validation as a separate hardening change.

**Minor: duplicate volume names cause silent overwrite**

If `VolumeMounts` contains two entries with the same `Name`, the first is silently dropped — the `requestIndex` also only reflects the final occurrence. Callers providing malformed requests with duplicate names get no signal that an entry was ignored. Consider warning when a name is overwritten.

**The warning message is misleading for the empty-path case**

When `!ok` (volume name not found in VolumeMounts), this log is accurate. But when `ok` is true and `GetContainerPath() == ""`, the warning says "no VolumeMount for volume" — which is wrong; the volume *does* have a VolumeMount entry, it just has an empty path. Consider splitting the two cases for more precise debugging.

<!-- cubesandbox-auto-review:start -->
## PR Review: refactor(one-click): unify MySQL/Redis config into one variable set

**Overall:** A well-structured refactoring that collapses two parallel config
sets into one. The three-way merge design, managed/external semantics, and
deprecation shim are carefully implemented. Below are findings worth addressing.

---

### Noteworthy findings

**1. Security: sequential `remove_env_kv` calls in `persist_unified_dep_config`** (lib/common.sh:1027-1032)

The loop calls `remove_env_kv` once per legacy key, each performing a full
`grep` + `mktemp` + read-rewrite + `mv`. On a low-end VM with burstable IOPS
or a heavily loaded filesystem this multiplies the write cost 8× for a single
cleanup step. A single-pass filter (awk, sed, or a bash loop that builds one
regex) would avoid the repeated atomic rewrites.

**2. `remove_env_kv` CRLF edge case** (lib/common.sh:651)

The new `remove_env_kv` uses `read -r` which does not strip `\r`. If a CRLF
env file reaches this function, the `\r` survives on every non-deleted line.
The key-prefix delete works (bash `*` glob matches through `\r`), but other
lines retain `\r`, which could confuse downstream tools. Tag the `\r` stripping
onto the read loop (`line="${line%%$'\r'}"`).

**3. Chinese README missing boolean alias docs** (README_zh.md:278)

The implementation (`_dep_is_managed`) accepts `true`/`yes`/`on`/`false`/`no`
/`off` in addition to `1`/`0`/`auto`, but the Chinese README only lists the
latter. The English README correctly documents all accepted values — please
update the Chinese version for parity.

**4. Self-build-deploy doc outdated "Docker Compose" wording** (docs/guide/self-build-deploy.md:11)

> "MySQL and Redis managed via Docker Compose"

This pre-dates the systemd migration; MySQL/Redis are now managed as
individual Docker containers under systemd (`cube-sandbox-mysql.service`,
`cube-sandbox-redis.service`), not via `docker compose`. Update to reflect
the current architecture.

---

### Minor / informational

- The EXIT trap overwrite in `check_external_deps_preflight` (install.sh:398)
  replaces the outer `WORK_DIR` cleanup trap — pre-existing, not introduced
  by this PR, but should be fixed (save/restore with `trap -p EXIT`).
- The `MIRROR=` empty-value write to `.one-click.env` (install.sh:1117) is
  harmless noise; adding a `[[ -n "${MIRROR:-}" ]]` guard would keep the
  env file clean.
<!-- cubesandbox-auto-review:end -->

item.body:
Previously the database and cache were described by two parallel variable sets: CUBE_SANDBOX_* for the bundled local containers and a separate CUBE_EXTERNAL_* set for an existing server. Operators had to know which set applied to their mode, credentials were duplicated across both, and switching between local and external meant editing a different group of variables.

Collapse everything onto a single CUBE_SANDBOX_{MYSQL,REDIS}_* set that describes the dependency in either mode. The *_HOST value selects the mode (a loopback address means the bundled container, any remote address means an external server), while a separate *_MANAGED flag decides whether cube owns the container. This cleanly supports the previously awkward case of an operator running their own MySQL/Redis on the local host without cube starting a conflicting container on the same port.

The resolved managed/external decision is frozen at install time so that later runtime and health-check scripts agree on it instead of recomputing an ambiguous default.

The legacy CUBE_EXTERNAL_* names remain honoured through a deprecation-warning alias shim that preserves their old semantics, so existing deployments keep working while new configs move to the unified names. Documentation, examples, and tests are updated to match.

review_comments.body:
**Bug: `[:space:]` POSIX character class does not match whitespace inside a `case` (glob) pattern**

In bash, `case` patterns use POSIX glob matching, not regex. The `[:space:]` character class is only interpreted by bracket expressions inside `[[ ... == pattern ]]` or `[[ ... =~ pattern ]]` contexts. Inside a `case` pattern's `[...]` bracket expression, `[:space:]` is treated as **literal characters** — matching `:`, `s`, `p`, `a`, `c`, `e` — not whitespace.

This means a credential component containing a space, tab, or newline would **silently pass through** this guard and produce a corrupted DSN that could be exploited if injected into a `bash -c` command (CWE-78).

Fix: use a `[[ ... =~ ... ]]` regex test instead:
```bash
if [[ "${_dsn_part}" =~ [@:/#%\"\`\$\'\\[[:space:]] ]]; then
  die "..."
fi
```

Same issue exists in `cube-api-start.sh:46`.

review_comments.body:
**Bug: `[:space:]` POSIX character class does not match whitespace inside a `case` (glob) pattern**

In bash, `case` patterns use POSIX glob matching, not regex. The `[:space:]` character class is only interpreted by bracket expressions inside `[[ ... == pattern ]]` or `[[ ... =~ pattern ]]` contexts. Inside a `case` pattern's `[...]` bracket expression, `[:space:]` is treated as **literal characters** — matching `:`, `s`, `p`, `a`, `c`, `e` — not whitespace.

This means a credential component containing a space, tab, or newline would **silently pass through** this guard and produce a corrupted DSN.

Fix: use a `[[ ... =~ ... ]]` regex test instead:
```bash
if [[ "${_dsn_part}" =~ [@:/#%\"\`\$\'\\[[:space:]] ]]; then
  die "..."
fi
```

Same issue exists in `cube-api-start.sh:46`.

review_comments.body:
**`remove_env_kv` prefix match silently misses indented keys & CRLF lines**

The authoritative delete loop at line 651 uses `[[ "${line}" == "${key}="* ]]` to match. This requires the line to start exactly with the key — it won't match lines with leading whitespace (e.g., `  CUBE_EXTERNAL_MYSQL_PASSWORD=secret` from a hand-edited file). Additionally, `read -r` does not strip `\r`, so CRLF-formatted lines carry a trailing `\r`. The `*` glob DOES match through the `\r`, so CRLF values are properly deleted, but the surviving non-matching lines in the file still retain their `\r` suffix.

Consider standardizing line ending handling across the env file read/write helpers. A minimal fix would strip `\r` in the read loop:
```bash
while IFS= read -r line || [[ -n "${line}" ]]; do
  line="${line%%$'\r'}"  # strip CR from CRLF
  ...
done
```

+# later scripts (postcheck/quickcheck) would recompute MANAGED=auto -> managed
+# and health-check a container that was never started.
+persist_unified_dep_config() {
+  local runtime_env_file="$1"
+  local operator_env_file="$2"
+
+  if mysql_is_external; then
+    upsert_env_kv "${runtime_env_file}" "CUBE_SANDBOX_MYSQL_HOST" "${CUBE_SANDBOX_MYSQL_HOST}"
+    upsert_env_kv "${runtime_env_file}" "CUBE_SANDBOX_MYSQL_PORT" "${CUBE_SANDBOX_MYSQL_PORT}"
+    upsert_env_kv "${runtime_env_file}" "CUBE_SANDBOX_MYSQL_USER" "${CUBE_SANDBOX_MYSQL_USER}"
+    upsert_env_kv "${runtime_env_file}" "CUBE_SANDBOX_MYSQL_PASSWORD" "${CUBE_SANDBOX_MYSQL_PASSWORD}"
+    upsert_env_kv "${runtime_env_file}" "CUBE_SANDBOX_MYSQL_DB" "${CUBE_SANDBOX_MYSQL_DB}"
+    upsert_env_kv "${runtime_env_file}" "CUBE_SANDBOX_MYSQL_MANAGED" "0"
+  else
+    upsert_env_kv "${runtime_env_file}" "CUBE_SANDBOX_MYSQL_MANAGED" "1"
+  fi
+
+  # DATABASE_URL points CubeAPI at the database.
+  #
+  # Managed (bundled) mode ALWAYS reassembles DATABASE_URL from the unified
+  # CUBE_SANDBOX_MYSQL_* vars and ignores any explicit operator DATABASE_URL.
+  # This is deliberate and matches the pre-unification behaviour: the bundled
+  # container is created with the CUBE_SANDBOX_MYSQL_* credentials, so an explicit
+  # DATABASE_URL (which for years shipped as an *active* default line in
+  # env.example, `mysql://cube:cube_pass@127.0.0.1:3306/cube_mvp`) must NOT be
+  # allowed to win -- an operator who customised CUBE_SANDBOX_MYSQL_PASSWORD but
+  # left that stale default line would otherwise point CubeAPI at the wrong
+  # password while the container/CubeMaster use the custom one.
+  #
+  # External mode honours an explicit operator DATABASE_URL so a fully custom DSN
+  # (extra params, a non-mysql scheme, ...) can be supplied; otherwise it is
+  # assembled from the unified vars. Read the operator's .env directly so a
+  # previously auto-generated value (carried in the upgrade merge / runtime env)
+  # is still refreshed from current settings.
+  local explicit_database_url=""
+  if mysql_is_external && [[ -n "${operator_env_file}" && -f "${operator_env_file}" ]]; then
+    explicit_database_url="$(read_env_key "${operator_env_file}" DATABASE_URL)"
+  fi
+  if [[ -n "${explicit_database_url}" ]]; then
+    upsert_env_kv "${runtime_env_file}" "DATABASE_URL" "${explicit_database_url}"
+  else
+    # Percent-encode every component so URL metacharacters (@ : / # %) cannot
+    # corrupt the connection string. In managed mode the bundled container always
+    # publishes on 127.0.0.1 (the compose template hardcodes the loopback bind)
+    # and conf.yaml is left at its 127.0.0.1 default (patch_cubemaster_external_deps
+    # only runs for external deps), so the DATABASE_URL host must be 127.0.0.1 too
+    # -- pinning it keeps CubeAPI and CubeMaster consistent even when *_HOST is a
+    # non-127.0.0.1 loopback literal (e.g. 127.0.0.2). Only an external dep uses
+    # the configured host verbatim.
+    local database_url_host_src="127.0.0.1"
+    mysql_is_external && database_url_host_src="${CUBE_SANDBOX_MYSQL_HOST}"
+    local database_url_user database_url_pass database_url_host
+    local database_url_port database_url_db
+    database_url_user="$(urlencode "${CUBE_SANDBOX_MYSQL_USER}")"
+    database_url_pass="$(urlencode "${CUBE_SANDBOX_MYSQL_PASSWORD}")"
+    database_url_host="$(urlencode "${database_url_host_src}")"
+    database_url_port="$(urlencode "${CUBE_SANDBOX_MYSQL_PORT}")"
+    database_url_db="$(urlencode "${CUBE_SANDBOX_MYSQL_DB}")"
+    upsert_env_kv "${runtime_env_file}" "DATABASE_URL" "mysql://${database_url_user}:${database_url_pass}@${database_url_host}:${database_url_port}/${database_url_db}"
+  fi
+
+  # Persist the unified Redis config. cube-proxy reads CUBE_PROXY_REDIS_* from the
+  # env file when rendering global.conf (CubeMaster reads the patched conf.yaml).
+  # As with MySQL, freeze the resolved MANAGED decision so later runtime scripts
+  # do not recompute auto differently for a loopback external service.
+  if redis_is_external; then
+    upsert_env_kv "${runtime_env_file}" "CUBE_SANDBOX_REDIS_HOST" "${CUBE_SANDBOX_REDIS_HOST}"
+    upsert_env_kv "${runtime_env_file}" "CUBE_SANDBOX_REDIS_PORT" "${CUBE_SANDBOX_REDIS_PORT}"
+    upsert_env_kv "${runtime_env_file}" "CUBE_SANDBOX_REDIS_PASSWORD" "${CUBE_SANDBOX_REDIS_PASSWORD}"
+    upsert_env_kv "${runtime_env_file}" "CUBE_PROXY_REDIS_IP" "${CUBE_SANDBOX_REDIS_HOST}"
+    upsert_env_kv "${runtime_env_file}" "CUBE_PROXY_REDIS_PORT" "${CUBE_SANDBOX_REDIS_PORT}"
+    upsert_env_kv "${runtime_env_file}" "CUBE_PROXY_REDIS_PASSWORD" "${CUBE_SANDBOX_REDIS_PASSWORD}"
+    upsert_env_kv "${runtime_env_file}" "CUBE_SANDBOX_REDIS_MANAGED" "0"
+  else
+    upsert_env_kv "${runtime_env_file}" "CUBE_SANDBOX_REDIS_MANAGED" "1"
+  fi
+
+  # Strip any lingering pre-unification CUBE_EXTERNAL_* keys from the runtime
+  # env. On upgrade the merge already drops them, but a fresh install seeded from
+  # an operator .env that still carries CUBE_EXTERNAL_* would otherwise persist a
+  # stale (now-migrated) external address/password on disk. Their values have
+  # already been folded into the CUBE_SANDBOX_* vars written above.
+  # Legacy key list is shared with apply_deprecated_external_aliases via the
+  # canonical ONE_CLICK_LEGACY_EXTERNAL_ALIAS_PAIRS array (validation.sh); take
+  # the "old" half of each old:new pair so the two paths never diverge.

+#
+# The whole IPv4 127.0.0.0/8 range is loopback, so any 127.x.y.z literal (with
+# in-range octets) matches, not just 127.0.0.1. A zone/scope ID suffix
+# (e.g. ::1%lo, 127.0.0.1%eth0) or a compressed IPv6 form other than ::1
+# (e.g. 0:0::1) will NOT match and is treated as non-loopback. Deployments
+# target IPv4, so that IPv6 gap is an accepted limitation rather than an
+# oversight.
+_host_is_loopback() {
+  local host="${1:-}"
+  case "${host}" in
+    "" | localhost | ::1 | 0:0:0:0:0:0:0:1)
+      return 0
+      ;;
+  esac
+  # Any 127.0.0.0/8 literal is loopback. Match the dotted-quad shape, then
+  # range-check the octets so e.g. 127.999.0.1 or a "127."-prefixed hostname
+  # is not misclassified.

+    (( 10#${b} <= 255 && 10#${c} <= 255 && 10#${d} <= 255 )) && return 0
+  fi

+# separate concern from where clients connect (*_HOST), so a user-run service on
+# 127.0.0.1:<port> can be used without cube starting a conflicting container.
+#   <unset>/auto    -> managed iff the host is loopback
+#   1/true/yes/on   -> force managed (host must be loopback, else hard error)
+#   0/false/no/off  -> force unmanaged (connect to an existing service)

+# exit the subshell and the error would be swallowed.

+      ;;
+    0 | false | no | off)

item.body:
Building the Docker builder image from mainland China often stalls or
fails when installing clang-14, because llvm.sh and the clang-14 apt
packages are pulled directly from apt.llvm.org, which is slow and
unreliable there. Contributors had no supported way to redirect those
downloads to a faster, China-reachable source.

Add an opt-in MIRROR=cn switch (with an overridable mirror host) that
routes the llvm.sh installer and the clang-14 packages through a China
mirror, while leaving the upstream apt.llvm.org path as the default so
existing builds are unaffected. The LLVM GPG signing key is still
fetched from apt.llvm.org, since that URL is hardcoded and the mirror
does not serve the key; this is a small request that generally succeeds
even when bulk downloads do not.

This build-time MIRROR is intentionally separate from the runtime
MIRROR=cn used by deploy/one-click. Documentation in both English and
Chinese is updated so the new option is discoverable.

<!-- cubesandbox-auto-review:start -->
## PR #941 Review — `refactor(sdk/go): dedup encodeConnectEnvelope and fix data-plane bugs`

### Overall

This is a well-structured refactor. The extraction of a shared `connect.go` eliminates the duplicated `encodeConnectEnvelope` and consolidates Connect wire-format helpers that were previously scattered across `envd.go` and `pty.go`. The bug fixes are clearly described, and each has a corresponding test assertion or new test case.

Test coverage in `pty_test.go` is thorough, including happy-path streaming, idle timeout, disconnect, context cancellation, compressed-frame rejection, end-stream trailer errors, base64 decode errors, and the new `exitCodeFromStatus` / `recordEnd` fallback logic.

### Bug fixes verified

| Bug | Fix | Verified? |
|-----|-----|-----------|
| `encodeConnectEnvelope` duplication | Extracted to `connect.go` with a single `io.Reader`-based definition | Clean dedup, `envd.go` and `pty.go` both reuse it |
| Envd RPCs 404 | Added `EnvdPort = 49983` in `sandbox.go` | `newEnvdRequest` now uses `s.GetHost(EnvdPort)` |
| exit-0 "missing exit code" | `processEndEvent.exitCode()` recovers from `status`/`exited` | Tested via `parseProcessStartStream` end-event path; PTY side tested via `recordEnd` |
| `CreateSnapshot("")` 422 | Always sends `map[string]any{}` instead of nil body | Verified in `TestSnapshotLifecycle` test body check |

### Noteworthy findings

**1. Redundant error branching in `readConnectEnvelope` (connect.go:46–51)**

The EOF/UnexpectedEOF check and the generic return are identical. This is misleading — the distinction exists at the source level but produces the same result. Would consolidate to a single `return 0, nil, err`.

**2. Asymmetric status-string parsing between command and PTY paths**

- `processEndEvent.exitCode()` in `envd.go:589` handles only the `"exit status N"` prefix pattern.
- `exitCodeFromStatus()` in `pty.go:577` uses regex and also handles `"exited with code N"`, `"signal N"` → 128+N, `"terminated by signal N"`, and plain `"exited"`.

The PTY path calls both (`recordEnd` → `exitCode()` then `exitCodeFromStatus()` then `Exited` fallback), so it's protected. The command path only calls `exitCode()`. For commands, signal deaths produce non-zero exit codes that proto3 JSON would serialize (not omitted like zero), so this works today — but the asymmetry adds maintenance risk if the field semantics evolve.

**3. No direct unit test file for `connect.go`**

`encodeConnectEnvelope`, `readConnectEnvelope`, and `parseConnectEndStream` are exercised indirectly through `pty_test.go`, but there's no dedicated test for edge cases: empty payload round-trip, oversized payload (>64 MiB), or `parseConnectEndStream` with `{}` / `{"error":null}` / non-JSON payloads. A small `connect_test.go` would close this gap.

### Minor notes

- `encodeConnectEnvelope` pre-sizes its buffer to `5+len(payload)` — avoids reallocation in the hot path.
- `ptyStreamControl.reset()` only stamps a timestamp without touching the timer — allocation-free hot path.
- The `cancel` field on `PtyHandle` ensures the stream context is cleaned up in `readLoop`'s defer, fixing a latent context leak.
- The `sandbox.go` const block comment clearly documents the JupyterPort/EnvdPort split.

### Conclusion

The PR is well factored, the bugs are convincingly fixed, and the test coverage is appropriate. The points above are minor and don't block the review.

item.body:
## Summary

Started as eliminating the duplicated `encodeConnectEnvelope` between `envd.go` and `pty.go`, plus three additional data-plane bug fixes uncovered while validating the change against a live sandbox.

## Changes

### Dedup & refactor
- New `connect.go` holds the shared Connect streaming wire-format: `encodeConnectEnvelope` (unified to `io.Reader`), `readConnectEnvelope`, `parseConnectEndStream`, protocol constants, and the `connectError`/`connectEndStream` types.
- `envd.go` drops its duplicate definitions and uses the shared encoder; `defaultEnvdUser` moved back to `envd.go` (it is envd auth, not Connect protocol).
- New `pty.go` adds the PTY namespace (Create/Connect/Kill/SendStdin/Resize + stream control), reusing the shared encoder instead of redefining it.

### Bug fixes
| # | Bug | Root cause | Fix |
|---|-----|-----------|-----|
| 0 | `encodeConnectEnvelope` duplicated between `envd.go` and `pty.go` with different signatures (`io.Reader` vs `*bytes.Buffer`) | no shared Connect wire-format module | Extract into `connect.go` with a single `io.Reader` definition; both files reuse it |
| 1 | All envd RPCs 404 | `newEnvdRequest` targeted `JupyterPort` (49999) | Add `EnvdPort=49983` and route envd RPCs there (matches Python/Node SDK `ENVD_PORT`); RunCode stays on 49999 |
| 2 | exit-0 commands report "missing exit code" | envd omits a zero-valued `exitCode` in proto3 JSON | Recover the code from the end event's `status`/`exited` fields |
| 3 | `CreateSnapshot("")` returns 422 | empty name sent a nil body, parsed as `null` | Always send a JSON object body (also unblocks `Clone`/`Rollback`) |

## Tests
- Unit tests added for the PTY data-plane requests, the shared envelope encoder (bytes + round-trip), exit-0 recovery, and the envd port / snapshot-body assertions.
- `go build`, `go vet`, and `go test ./...` all pass.

review_comments.body:
**Potential memory exhaustion risk via wire-triggered allocation**

`readConnectEnvelope` allocates `make([]byte, size)` on line 57 before the body is read, with `size` coming from 5 header bytes on the wire. `maxConnectEnvelopeSize` is 64 MB, so an attacker who can influence the TCP stream can trigger a 64 MB heap allocation per frame header without sending the body — just 5 bytes per attempt. Repeated ~20 times, this is 1.28 GB in heap allocations.

Consider reducing `maxConnectEnvelopeSize` to a value aligned with the largest legitimate payload (e.g. 10 MB), or using a progressive read strategy / `sync.Pool` to avoid large per-message allocation spikes.

The timeout-error message on line 346 could then mask a user-initiated disconnect. Fix by acquiring `c.mu` once and reading both `c.disc` and `c.fired` atomically. The comment on line 329 states the locking "prevent[s]" this, but the two separate method calls each acquire and release the lock, creating a non-atomic window.

**No fallback timeout on unary PTY calls** — `SendStdin`, `Resize`, and `Kill` each call `p.unary()`, which has no client-side timeout beyond whatever the caller passes via `ctx`. If a caller passes `context.Background()`, a hung envd response pins the goroutine indefinitely. `Create` and `Connect` apply `defaultPtyTimeout` (60s) as a fallback; the unary methods should too — either by plumbing `PtyConnectOptions` into them or by wrapping the context with a default timeout internally.

The `streamCtx` cancel function (from line 361's `context.WithCancel`) is never called when `readLoop` exits normally after receiving an end-stream. The defers close channels, the body, and the idle timer, but not the context. While this does not cause a goroutine leak, it keeps the derived context tree alive until the `PtyHandle` is garbage-collected. ## PR #940 — Transparent deletion of paused sandboxes

### Overview

This PR implements automatic resume-before-delete for paused sandboxes across three service layers (Cubelet → CubeMaster → CubeAPI), with appropriate error propagation, `Retry-After` headers, and comprehensive test coverage. The design is sound and the implementation is production-quality.

---

### Key Strengths

1. **Crash-safe sync ordering** — The converged RUNNING state is persisted *before* the delete marker, so a crash between the two syncs leaves a running (not paused, not half-deleted) sandbox.
2. **TOCTOU correctness** — The lifecycle lock protects against a sandbox transitioning from RUNNING→PAUSED between the initial state read and the destroy workflow. The state is re-read under the lock.
3. **Robust deadline budget** — The proportional split with clamping prevents degenerate allocations at all remaining-time values.
4. **End-to-end error consistency** — Each business code flows through `isDeleteAutoResumeBusinessCode` → `map_delete_cubemaster_err` with the correct HTTP status and `Retry-After` header.
5. **Thorough test coverage** — Every failure mode (pausing rejection, deadline exhaustion, shim timeout, reconciliation, persistence failure, lock contention) is tested, and the running-sandbox path is verified to be unchanged.

---

### Actionable Suggestions

**1. Extract shared response-reserve helper** (`delete_resume.go:51` and `delete_resume.go:204`)

The `remaining/6` clamped-to-`[1s, 5s]` computation is duplicated in `newDeleteDeadlineBudget` and `deleteLifecycleLockDeadline`. A small helper would keep them consistent if the formula evolves.

**2. Add explanatory comment for error code conflation** (`service.go:590`)

`ErrorCode_TaskResumeFailed` is used for three distinct scenarios: (a) insufficient RPC response time before even trying the lock, (b) the resume RPC itself failed, and (c) persisted-state sync failed. All three produce the same HTTP 503 with a 5-second retry, so the external contract is identical, but a comment would help operators reading logs understand that case (a) is not a resume attempt.

**3. Move `syncCtx` inside the `if opts.persist` block** (`update.go:290`)

`syncCtx` is allocated on every call to `resumeLocked` but only used when `opts.persist` is true (i.e., the explicit resume path). For the delete path (`persist=false`), this is a dead allocation. Minor tidiness.

---

### Minor Observations

- The 1/6 and 1/4 proportional split ratios (`delete_resume.go:51-52`) are opaque without a comment explaining the rationale.
- The handler `#[utoipa::path]` annotation (`handlers/sandboxes.rs:204`) describes 503 with the same wording as `openapi.yml` but omits the explicit `Retry-After` value mention (2s / 5s) from the description text.
- `release_paused_resources_test.go` was correctly simplified: the `admitResume` signature change (dropping the response parameter that was only written by admission errors) removed the need for test code that constructed a dummy `UpdateCubeSandboxResponse`.

---

### No Critical Issues Found

- No security concerns — the lifecycle lock and TOCTOU guards prevent any bypass of the existing state machine.
- No performance regressions — running-sandbox delete retains the existing fast path; the new lock-and-resume overhead only applies to paused sandboxes, and is bounded by the deadline budget.
- No test coverage gaps — all code paths are covered, including the reconciliation case where the shim proves RUNNING despite an RPC error.
- Documentation is accurate and consistent between the English and Chinese lifecycle guides and the OpenAPI spec.

item.body:
## Motivation

Deleting a paused sandbox currently fails because the runtime rejects the normal delete operation while the VM is paused. Users must manually resume the sandbox before deleting it.

This PR makes `DELETE /sandboxes/{sandboxID}` work for a stable paused CubeBox. The sandbox is resumed as part of the delete operation and then removed through the existing destroy workflow. DELETE remains synchronous: success is returned only after cleanup completes.

## Design

CubeMaster remains the external DELETE entry point and continues to coordinate both synchronous and asynchronous destroy requests. The atomic resume-before-destroy transition is implemented in Cubelet's `Destroy` path.

Cubelet owns the authoritative runtime state, containerd task, and the per-sandbox lifecycle lock shared by pause, resume, rollback, and commit. Only paused or pausing Cube runtime deletes enter this bounded gate, so running deletes retain their existing direct path. Keeping the transition in Cubelet keeps state inspection, resume, reconciliation, and normal cleanup together.

This supersedes the API-only paused-delete workaround in #831. That workaround translated a CubeMaster internal error into `409 Conflict` after an extra sandbox-status lookup. This PR removes that fallback: DELETE now performs the bounded wake-up itself and returns typed capacity or retryable lifecycle errors only when the actual wake-up cannot proceed.

## Behavior

- A stable `PAUSED` sandbox is resumed internally, then follows the normal destroy workflow.
- A `RUNNING` sandbox keeps the existing delete path and does not resume.
- If a resume RPC reports an error but runtime reconciliation proves the VM is `RUNNING`, DELETE continues. Otherwise the sandbox remains retryable.
- The internal wake-up is bounded to 5 seconds, with 20 seconds reserved for cleanup and 5 seconds reserved for the Cubelet RPC response. The existing CubeAPI 30-second request timeout is unchanged.
- DELETE does not emit a caller-visible `sandbox.resumed` event, reset idle timeout, or create a background retry.

## Error Semantics

DELETE for running sandbox and existing `404` behavior are unchanged. For the paused-delete path:

- Capacity or missing resource error returns `409 Conflict`.
- `PAUSING` or another lifecycle operation in progress returns `503` with `Retry-After: 2`.
- A failed or unproven internal resume, or insufficient remaining Cubelet RPC budget, returns `503` with `Retry-After: 5`.

`Retry-After: 5` follows CubeProxy's existing auto-resume failure backoff, while `Retry-After: 2` follows its PAUSING gate. These headers tell the client when to retry; DELETE is not continued or retried in the background.

## Scope

This PR does not add a public DELETE parameter or protobuf field, bypass resume admission, change the existing CubeShim delete guard, alter ordinary running DELETE behavior, or add a new metric.

## Validation

Focused Linux builder checks passed:

```bash
cd Cubelet && go test ./pkg/utils -run TestResourceLock -count=1
cd Cubelet && go test ./services/cubebox -run 'TestResumeTaskLocked|TestDeleteAutoResume|TestDestroy' -count=1
cd CubeMaster && go test ./pkg/service/sandbox -run TestSetSyncDestroyFailure -count=1
cd CubeAPI && cargo test --locked
cd CubeAPI && cargo test --locked delete_paused_sandbox_maps_business_errors_from_cubemaster
```

The full CubeAPI suite completed with `88 passed; 0 failed`. The focused HTTP route test verifies CubeMaster `130409` -> HTTP `409`, alongside the `503` and `Retry-After` cases.

Real-server validation built and atomically deployed the final Cubelet, CubeMaster, and CubeAPI binaries. All three services remained active and both health endpoints returned success.

Live E2E validation created a temporary sandbox, paused it, and deleted it directly without an explicit `resume` or `connect` request:

- pause returned `204`, and GET reported `paused`;
- DELETE returned `204 No Content` in `629 ms`;
- subsequent GET returned `404`;
- no matching containerd task or sandbox data path remained.

## References

Fixes #219.

Replaces the API-only paused-delete workaround from #831.

1. **Line 293**: `firstContainer == nil || firstContainer.Container == nil` — returns TaskResumeFailed. The `fakeDestroyContainer` already has a `taskErr` field, making this easy to test.

Raw gRPC / connection errors (e.g. "connection reset", ttrpc status strings) from the Cubelet reach the API client as the `message` field of the HTTP response body. Consider wrapping non-business-code errors in a sanitized generic message like "sync delete failed" before forwarding to the client, and logging the full `err.Error()` server-side.

The `LockContext` method polls `TryLock` every 5ms via a ticker. Under contention, this produces up to 400 failed CAS attempts over the 2s `deleteLifecycleLockMaxWait` window. Since contention is per-sandbox-key and rare in practice this is acceptable, but consider adding an exponential backoff (e.g. doubling from 1ms to ~100ms) to reduce CPU waste during sustained contention — for example from a bulk-delete storm on a shared lifecycle operation.

needsPausedPreflight is computed from a status read taken before acquiring  sandboxLifecycleLocks. If the sandbox is observed as  RUNNING at that point (so  needsPausedPreflight == false), the request skips the lock
entirely and falls straight through to  engine.Destroy(...) unprotected. If a concurrent  Update(pause) wins  sandboxLifecycleLocks and pauses the sandbox in the gap between that read and the actual destroy call, this Destroy request ends up doing a plain destroy against what is now a paused sandbox — the exact scenario this PR is meant to guard against — and it does so without holding the lock at all.

unconditionally on entry (before reading status) and deciding the resume-vs-plain-destroy branch under the lock, rather than deciding whether to lock based on a stale read? **Race window between state check and lock acquisition**

`needsPausedPreflight` is evaluated at line 595-596 from a `Get()` at line 581, but the lifecycle lock isn't acquired until line 609. Between these lines, a concurrent pause operation could transition the sandbox from `RUNNING` to `PAUSING`/`PAUSED`. Since `needsPausedPreflight` was computed as `false`, the preflight block (and its lock acquisition) is skipped entirely, and the destroy proceeds on a now-paused sandbox without the auto-resume preflight.

The state re-read under the lock at line 620 mitigates the reverse race (stale `true` → re-read discovers running), but the `false` → skip case is not caught because the entire locked section is gated on `needsPausedPreflight`.

**Suggestion:** Either (a) move the `needsPausedPreflight` evaluation inside the locked section after the re-read, or (b) acquire the lifecycle lock unconditionally when the sandbox is in a Cube runtime and re-evaluate the state under the lock.
